This document compiles the nationally determined contributions on climate change mitigation and adaptation presented by the Venezuelan State, prepared together with People's Power, the interministerial team, State enterprises, the education, academic and research sectors, as well as the private sector. This document was prepared within the framework of the actions of the Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela under the Gran Misión Madre Tierra Venezuela, in its Vertex 4 “Climate for life” and the 6T. SIXTH TRANSFORMATION: ECOSOCIALISM, SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY, of the ORGANIC LAW OF THE HOMELAND PLAN OF THE 7 GREAT TRANSFORMATIONS (2025-2031).

Foreword

The SECOND NATIONALLY DETERMINED CONTRIBUTION (NDC) OF THE BOLIVARIAN REPUBLIC OF VENEZUELA 2025-2030 is a document that sets out the commitment to combat climate change that the Republic presents within the framework of the Paris Agreement (2015), with the firm decision to reduce our greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, adapt to the impacts of climate change and learn to manage life in the face of this change in a sovereign manner.

Regarding mitigation, in order to reduce emissions and strengthen our already favorable condition of net reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2) equivalent and maintain carbon neutrality, concrete actions are defined in 37 projects to be carried out in sectors such as energy, transport, agriculture, industry, increasing reforested area, and strengthening and implementing renewable energy generation capacities.

Regarding adaptation, actions are incorporated in 41 projects, such as adjustments in the redesign of cities and accessibility to public services, protection of vulnerable families who might settle in risk zones, establishment of a national network of rain gauge stations in the country's 5338 communes for the measurement, reporting and analysis of data whose results can be applied in the preparation of communal risk maps, and protection of national parks and other areas under special administration regime. All of this with the intense and ongoing participation of the organized people.

Many of these actions will be financed with public resources and developed through popular consultation processes to select the projects prioritized in elections and executed directly by the communes; others require international financing.

All of this is set out in a structural strategy contained in the Gran Misión Madre Tierra Venezuela created by President Nicolás Maduro, which includes seven vertices of action to be developed in the social, spatial-territorial, economic, cultural and environmental spheres in order to plan and manage in the face of climate change impacts, provide security to the population and meet its needs with deep respect for Mother Earth.

ORGANIZATION AND TRAINING FOR LIFE. Activation and training of ecosocialist leaders in order to encourage the formation of Ecosocialism Councils in the 5338 Communes.

SOWING FOR LIFE. Organized planting to reforest degraded areas, protect watershed headwaters and establish productive plantations. Building capacities in seed collection, as well as nursery development and management.

TERRITORY FOR LIFE. Delineation of river basins; identify in each commune or communal circuit the respective micro-watershed and build the 5.338 Risk Maps; update or create the management plans and use regulations in the 408 areas under special regime (ABRAE).

CLIMATE FOR LIFE. Strengthen capacities for measuring, collecting and processing climate data throughout the national territory, for territorial planning and to undertake adaptation and mitigation actions in response to the processes affecting global warming. Prepare, from the communes, the national Adaptation and Mitigation plans in response to Global Warming.

WILDLIFE FOR LIFE. The protection and rational use of wild fauna, and updating of regulations for the capture, movement and national and international trade of animal species.

SANITATION FOR LIFE. Implement regulations that standardize the generation, collection, separation, reuse and final disposal of waste; establish the OPERATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT to promote and develop sustainable and professional waste management throughout the country and advance the transition toward a circular economy.

PRODUCTION FOR LIFE. Develop the Economic Transformation with an ecosocialist vision, pursuing the satisfaction of human needs with deep respect for nature.

Even under unilateral coercive measures that seek to economically strangle our nation, this inclusive and comprehensive national strategy is, without a doubt, the most ambitious nationally determined contribution ever put forward, and its implementation is only possible under conditions of unity between the organized people and the Government at all its levels.

Ricardo Molina Peñaloza Minister of People's Power for Ecosocialism

Let's not change the climate! Let's change the system! And consequently we will begin to save the planet Commander Hugo Rafael Chávez Frías Copenhagen, 2009

Chapter I. National Context

Geographic profile

The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela is located in northern South America, approximately between coordinates 00° 38’ 53” and 12°H’ 46” north latitude, and 59° 48’ 10” and 73° 25’ 00” west longitude. By territorial extent it ranks 7th among Latin American countries, with a continental and insular territory.

The Venezuelan geographic space has a land area of 1.075.945 km2, which includes 139.312 km2 of Guayana Esequiba. The aquatic space comprises more than 500.000 km2 distributed between the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean (27, 2% of the total surface of the Caribbean Sea), which includes the Territorial Sea, the Contiguous Zone and the projection of the Exclusive Economic Zone.

In its insular region, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has 311 islands, islets and cays, which together with Nueva Esparta state (the Islands of Margarita, Coche and Cubagua) make up the country's insular façade, with coastlines covering approximately 1.413 km. Owing to its territorial extent, it is the only South American country with coastlines open simultaneously to the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean.

The country's coastal zone occupies 143.587 km2and constitutes 10 % of the national territory. Its land strip reaches 58.507 km2, while its aquatic space extends over 85.080 km2, with a wide variety of aquatic environments and diversity of fishery resources. Approximately 4,2 million inhabitants are settled within it, representing 18,20% of the total national population.

Figure 1.1. Political-administrative division of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela

The country has four geographic façades, called the Caribbean, Atlantic, Andean and Amazonian. These give rise to political, economic and social relations of great importance for the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. In addition, these fronts facilitate land, sea and air transport and communications with all the countries of the American continent, the Caribbean and the world.

From a political-administrative standpoint, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela is divided into a Capital District, 2 4 states, 335 municipalities, 1.136 parishes and 311 islands, islets and cays that make up the federal dependencies. Guayana Esequiba state was created by the Organic Law for the Defense of Guayana Esequiba (Extraordinary Official Gazette No. 6.798 of 03 April 2024).

Environmental profile

Figure 1.2. Biological Diversity of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. Source: MINEC, 2024.

The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has great environmental potential thanks to its privileged geographic location in the intertropical zone of South America. In this context, the country lies at the intersection of the Andean, Amazonian, Caribbean and Guiana biogeographic regions. Its geographic location and geological history give it a natural diversity that grants it the status of a megadiverse country.

Its territorial extent of 1.075.945 km2 of mainland and more than 500.000 km2 of marine areas offers a wide range of environmental conditions that give rise to an impressive biological diversity, reflected in its 15 natural bioregions, ranging from the Coastal Cordillera to the Tepui System of the Guiana Shield, and placing the country among the top ten countries with the greatest biological diversity on the planet (Figure 1.2).

Therefore, the conservation of the country's megadiversity plays a crucial role in regulating the regional and global climate, so protecting it does not only mean guaranteeing the survival of the species that inhabit these ecosystems; rather, strategic actions must simultaneously be implemented to maintain ecosystems over time and the sustainable management of livelihoods. In this context, the organization of the country's geographic space is framed within a new development model under the principles of Ecosocialism, grounded in the Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, contained in Title III, Chapter 9: Environmental Rights (Articles 127, 128 and 129), and on the principle of Territorial Planning and ecosocialism that guides the socialist geographic spatial distribution of development; accordingly, the country's lands are managed around the Territorial Development Axes, the Strategic Defense and Development Regions, the Urban-Rural Systems, the Areas of Maximum Agricultural Preservation and the Areas Under Special Administration Regime (Briceño, 2023).

In response, the Venezuelan State carries out ecosocialist territorial management that advances in strengthening the National System of Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE), promoting policies, plans and programs as a strategic action for sustainable land-use planning and management with a gender, intergenerational, worldview and intercultural approach. Accordingly, a total of 408 Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE) have been decreed to date, occupying approximately 68,4% of the country's total area (Figure 1.3).

These areas are vital for resilience to climate change, the conservation of carbon sinks, the protection of endemic species and guaranteeing, over time, the conservation of ecosystems and the sustainable management of livelihoods.

Figure 1.3. Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE) of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. Source: MINEC, 2022.

Land classification

In the First Biennial Transparency Report (2024), the country classified land into six categories according to the IPCC (2006), namely: forest land, cropland, grassland, wetlands, settlements and other land (Figure 1.4), making it possible to advance in reporting on the Land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) sector, within the Transparency framework of the Paris Agreement.

For the year 2022, forest land represents 57,83% of the national territory, grassland represents 21,93% and is distributed among savannas, tropical and subtropical shrublands, and montane grassland cover; 87,13% of cropland corresponds to rainfed crops, mosaics, perennial associations and mixed crops; the remaining 12,87% of the area of these lands is distributed as follows: 3,72% in grain and legume crops (black beans, peas, beans and pigeon peas), 2,93% in cereal crops (rice, sorghum, maize and wheat), 2,05% in traditional tropical crops (coffee, cacao, sugarcane and tobacco), 1,66% in fruit trees, 1,30% in textile and oilseed crops, and 1,22% distributed among vegetable, root and tuber crops (MINEC, 2024).

As for Wetlands, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has a richness and diversity of wetlands, located in inland and marine-coastal waters, with permanent and temporary regimes, of the marine, estuarine, lagoon, riverine, palustrine and lacustrine types.

Comparatively, the regions of the Lake Maracaibo basin, La Guajira, the Deltana Platform and Paria are the most diverse. There are currently five Ramsar sites or habitats of international importance for wetland conservation (MINEC, 2010).

Forest heritage

The forests of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela represent 5,5% of the forest formations of South America and 1,2% of the world's forests (FAO, 2020).

The largest area of these forests (83%) is located south of the Orinoco River, in the Guayana region. They occupy 39%, 37% and 7% of the states of Bolívar, Amazonas and Delta Amacuro, respectively (FAO, 2020).

Figure 1.4. Land classification of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, according to IPCC methodology.

76% of the country's forests are located on the Guiana Shield, in the states of Amazonas and Bolívar, federal entities that represent 47,1% of the national territory. This region is one of the most pristine and biologically diverse areas (80,5%).

Within the country's ABRAE system, areas for the sustainable management of forest heritage make up 11,15% of the national land area (Figure 1.5), represented by 10 forest reserves (6.742.407,20 ha) and 43 protected forest areas (3.473.702,00 ha). There are also areas declared as forest lots, with a total area of 967.093,00 ha. All the aforementioned areas are administered by the National Environmental Authority (MINEC, 2022).

Figure 1.5. Forest land of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela

Water resources

The country is among the top 15 nations in freshwater reserves on the planet (Figure 1.6).

For the purposes of integrated water administration and management, the Venezuelan State divided the territory into sixteen (16) hydrographic regions, in accordance with article 7 of the Water Law.

Figure 1.6. Water Resources of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela

Demographic profile

The Venezuelan population grew by 39,7% between 2000 and 2024 (Figure 1.7).

Figure 1.7. Population projection 2000-2050. Source: INE, 2024.

For the year 2024, 89 % of the population is concentrated in urban areas and 11% is located in rural areas (Figure 1.8).

Figure 1.8. Rural and urban population of Venezuela

The country's population is mainly concentrated in the states of Zulia, Miranda, Carabobo, Lara, Bolívar and the Capital District (Figure 1.9).

Figure 1.9. Distribution of the Venezuelan population. Source: INE, 2024.

Indigenous Peoples

Venezuelan indigenous peoples account for approximately 2,8 % of the country's total population (Figure 1.10), and are located in greatest proportion in the northeast of the country, in Delta de Amacuro state, specifically in the Orinoco Delta, in the south of Bolívar state (border with Guyana and Brazil), Amazonas state (border with Brazil and Colombia), southwest of Apure state (border with Colombia) and northwest of Zulia state (border with Colombia).

Figure 1.10. Indigenous communities and territories of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. Source: INE, 2022.

Economic profile

The Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, in article 299, establishes that the country's socioeconomic system “is based on the principles of social justice, democracy, efficiency, free competition, environmental protection, productivity and solidarity, in order to ensure integral human development and a dignified and beneficial existence for the community”.

The Venezuelan economy is based mainly on export revenues from the oil, mining, steel and aluminum industries. However, with the aim of overcoming oil rentierism, the Venezuelan State is taking concrete actions to diversify the economy, within the framework of the development of 13 productive engines and the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations.

The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has suffered a significant decline in national income due to the imposition of 1.127 Unilateral Coercive Measures illegally imposed by the government of the United States of America (MPPP, 2024), and although this has represented a significant obstacle, the country has met almost all the objectives of the international environmental treaties, especially the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement.

Social profile

Human development, the fight against poverty and social inclusion are premises in permanent development in Venezuela. This has been achieved through programs created and financed by the Venezuelan State, called “Missions and Great Social Missions”, and the country continues to advance in building an egalitarian and just society. Venezuela has organized People's Power in 47 thousand communal councils and 5.336 Communal Circuits, which has made it possible to confront the effects of the Unilateral Coercive Measures (MPPP, 2024) and defend our sovereignty.

Productive profile

The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela is an oil, agricultural, forestry, fishing and tourism country and a producer of hydroelectric energy and ecosystem services.

It is a country in full industrial development, with an economy based on the extraction and refining of oil and other minerals, as well as multiple agricultural and industrial activities, in transition toward a diversified productive economy (MPPRE, 2024).

Chapter II. National circumstances and institutional arrangements

Socio-political profile

The Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela clearly and transparently establishes Environmental Rights (Chapter IX). Accordingly, the Venezuelan State adopts ecosocialism as a revolutionary doctrine and as a historical social model based on respect for the rights of Mother Earth and the good living of our people, developing the principle of unity within diversity, the integral and systemic vision, popular participation, the role of the Nation State, and the incorporation of technologies and forms of organization of production, distribution and consumption aimed at the rational, optimal and sustainable use of natural resources, respecting the processes and cycles of nature.

To this end, the geopolitical vision of the territorial structure and of the organization of the country's geographic space is fundamental, in accordance with a new development model under the principles of Ecosocialism, which has enabled substantive progress on the precepts established in the Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela contained in Title III, Chapter 9: Environmental Rights (Articles 127,128 and 129).

In addition, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has an important legal and regulatory framework that governs the implementation of policies, programs, plans and projects, and underpins the actions of the State aimed at climate change mitigation and adaptation, in order to address the conditions of vulnerability that will potentially affect the country.

Despite the adversities arising from the imposition of Unilateral Coercive Measures, the Venezuelan State has managed to consolidate itself as a carbon neutral country, according to the most recent National Greenhouse Gas Inventory. This achievement is part of global efforts to address the Global Climate Crisis, and reflects the country's commitment to the conservation of life on the planet, the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations, the Gran Misión Madre Tierra, the international agreements signed under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement. Carbon neutrality has been achieved thanks to the ecosocialist policies implemented, which include sustainable territorial management, where 68,4% of the national territory is under Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE), and to the implementation of national ecosystem and landscape restoration strategies, advances that reaffirm the commitment to and importance of shared environmental management and the participation of People's Power in building a development model in harmony with nature.

However, it is a country vulnerable to the effects of climate change. This has become evident with greater frequency over the last 25 years, with the occurrence of natural events associated with extraordinary hydrometeorological phenomena, which represents a significant socio-environmental risk in the national territory.

In this regard, the Venezuelan State, under the motto of the leader of the revolution Hugo Chávez Frías “let's not change the climate, let's change the system” (COP 15, 2009), has taken significant steps on climate change, in accordance with the Paris Agreement, the Sustainable Development Goals and the political commitment framed in the Homeland Plan (2019-2025), in the nation's fifth historic objective “Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species”, and in the sixth transformation “Ecosocialism”, established in the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, and in the seven vertices or lines of action of the Gran Misión Madre Tierra (Figure 2.1). In this context, Venezuela is advancing on its path of progress toward strengthening climate change institutions, notably: The creation of the Presidential Commission for Climate Change on a permanent basis, by Decree No. 4.612, published in the Official Gazette of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela No. 42.247 dated 3 November 2021 (Figure 2.2). Likewise, in February 2022 the Ministry of People's Power for Ecosocialism, as the National Authority with competence in environmental matters, incorporated into its organizational structure the Vice Ministry for the Preservation of Life and Biodiversity (Decree No. 4.635). This Vice Ministry coordinates five (5) General Directorates dedicated to adaptation, mitigation, climate change monitoring, and policies for strengthening and defending biological diversity. This has driven the country to take significant steps in fulfilling the agreements established under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Transparency Framework of the Paris Agreement (Figure 2.3).

Figure 2.1. Seven great transformations of the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan 2025-2031 and the vertices of the Gran Misión Madre Tierra.

Considering the above, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) three National Communications on Climate Change, published in 2005, 2017 and 2024; the first Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 2017) and its update (NDC 2021); and in 2024, at COP 29, the country submitted its First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR) and the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory document (DIN 1990-2022). Likewise, the process of collective construction of the Second Nationally Determined Contribution continued, making it possible to fulfill the commitment of the Third Round NDC 3.0 (2025).

This demonstrates the high political commitment of the Venezuelan State within the framework of the Paris Agreement, adopted through decision 1/CP.21.

Figure 2.2. Presidential Commission for Climate Change

Figure 2.3. National Path of Progress on Climate Change (1994-2030).

Planning and collective construction processes of the Second Nationally Determined Contribution 2025

Within a framework of shared management and environmental co-responsibility to confront the climate crisis, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela prepares the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) for the period 2025- 2030, based on a participatory and inclusive interministerial and multisectoral process with People's Power, whose climate action establishes cross-cutting elements of ecosystem-based Mitigation and Adaptation solutions with a gender, generational, worldview and intercultural approach, linked to the policies, plans, programs and projects of the Venezuelan State established in the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031 and in the seven vertices or lines of action of the Gran Misión Madre Tierra Venezuela, the Sustainable Development Goals and the current environmental legal framework; this will allow the country to advance in complying with the Paris Agreement and fight against the adverse effects of the global environmental crisis, as well as achieve the target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 20% by 2030. (Figure 2.4) This institutional arrangement made it possible to strengthen the work path in line with the lessons learned in preparing the First Nationally Determined Contribution (2017) and the update of the NDC in 2021. To achieve this, a participatory methodology was used for the process of formulating the Second NDC for the period 2025-2030, consisting of two key moments described in Figure 2.5. This implementation mechanism was designed according to the country's specific national circumstances, in line with the national policies linked to protagonistic and participatory democracy, and becomes a way of demonstrating the commitment of the Venezuelan State to take its first steps within the enhanced transparency framework (ETF); it therefore promotes progress in reporting under the principles of transparency, consistency, comparability, completeness and accuracy, which were established in decisions 1/CP.21, 4/CMA.l, 5/ CMA.3, 9/CMA.l and 18/CMA.1 This participatory and inclusive process with the interministerial and intersectoral team and People's Power consolidated a work path for strengthening the Second Nationally Determined Contribution 2025, which made it possible to:

Figure 2.4. Organizational structure of the 2nd NDC of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

  • Assess the negative impact of the Unilateral Coercive Measures (MCU) on progress of the NDC 2021.
  • Identify the mitigation and adaptation measures and actions with the greatest feasibility of implementation linked to the policies, plans, programs and projects of the Venezuelan State, the Sustainable Development Goals and the current environmental legal framework.
  • Establish cross-cutting elements of ecosystem-based Mitigation and Adaptation solutions with a gender, generational, worldview and intercultural approach.
  • Present greater ambition in the actions to be carried out in the territory, within a framework of shared management and co-responsibility, in implementing climate action based on a participatory and inclusive interministerial, multisectoral process with People's Power.
  • Establish synergies between the mitigation and adaptation components, which feed back into and reinforce the emission reduction objectives.
  • Establish mechanisms for tracking NDC progress, through outcome and tracking indicators under the SMART methodology.
  • Establish measures and actions based on the financial resources required, associated with the timing and implementation scenario in the period 2025-2030.

This represents a first step toward strengthening national capacities that makes it possible to progressively close gaps, seeking to provide sustainability over time to the general and specific procedures established in the modalities, procedures and guidelines (MPGs) and in decisions 1/ CP.21, 4/CMA.1, 5/CMA.3, 9/CMA.1 and 18/CMA.1, which strengthens the mechanisms for monitoring, evaluating and tracking the progress made in the formulation and fulfillment of the Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).

Progress of the NDCs in the Private sector

In the process of collective, participatory and inclusive construction of the Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) in 2024, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela began a process of awareness-raising and dissemination of the results of the country's vulnerability assessment in working groups with the private sector, which made it possible to learn about business initiatives linked to their environmental responsibility actions. This space motivated the sector to take a more active role in identifying and implementing climate change mitigation and adaptation solutions that contribute to increasing its competitiveness, capacity for innovation, resilience and management of the operational and financial impacts caused by climate-related events (reflected in loss and damage).

All of this seeks to consolidate cooperation alliances with the private sector that make it possible to establish the mechanisms of environmental management and co-responsibility set out in the current Organic Law of the Environment (Articles 94, 96, 97, 98 and 99), leading to strengthened strategic alliances of the National Environmental Authority (MINEO) in prior and subsequent control actions, linked to the implementation of mitigation and adaptation measures and actions, as part of the sector's environmental and social responsibility.

Figure 2.6. Representation of actions to achieve business resilience. Source: Adapted from Hernán, 2023.

Subsequently, following a process of environmental supervision and auditing by the governing body with competence in environmental matters (MINEC), Environmental Performance Certificates may be issued, which will certify compliance with environmental regulations, as well as with the measures and actions that increase business resilience to the effects of climate change (Figure 2.6).

It is a challenge for the State to record these actions and account for their impact in the country's progress reports, which will make it possible to establish dynamic multisectoral processes to align priorities and investments in order to achieve significant impacts in progressively increasing climate ambition. In this context, the Second Nationally Determined Contribution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela incorporates private sector initiatives on sustainable forest management (strategic alliance with MINEC), as well as enterprises for processing organic matter from urban and agro-industrial solid waste, intended for the production of substrates. Likewise, the promotion of climate-smart agroforestry systems in the Venezuelan Andes.

Likewise, this public-private articulation will make it possible, in the period 2025-2030, to design a cooperation roadmap in four cross-cutting dimensions covering key aspects of the NDC cycle (Figure 2.7).

Figure 2.7. Dimensions of public-private cooperation for the NDCs. as a basis for informing strategies and roadmaps. Source: Adapted from Hernán, 2023.

Chapter III. NDC Mitigation

The Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) on Mitigation was strengthened through a process of collective, participatory and inclusive construction, begun in 2024, which, through the evaluation of the NDC 2021 update, made it possible to determine the improvements to be applied in formulating the NDCs within the framework of the Third Round 2025, under the enhanced transparency framework, in accordance with decisions 4/CMA.l, 5/ CMA.3,18/CMA.l. This will make it possible to continue supporting global efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, in order to address climate change based on the principle of “common but differentiated responsibilities” (Figure 3.1). The work path for strengthening the Mitigation NDC made it possible to assess the negative impact of the Unilateral Coercive Measures (MCU) on progress of the NDC 2021; this situation led to identifying the measures and actions with the greatest feasibility of implementation linked to the policies, plans, programs and projects of the Venezuelan State, to the Sustainable Development Goals and to the key categories determined in the INGEI (2024), based on the financial resources required to achieve the emission reduction potential, associated with the timing and implementation scenario in the period 2025-2030. Therefore, the approach applied during the formulation of the mitigation component of the Second NDC made it possible to align the sectoral measures and actions of the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the Seven Great Transformations (2025- 2031), the seven vertices of the Gran Misión Madre Tierra Venezuela, the current environmental legislation and the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory, so that they can become a mechanism to contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals established in the 2030 Agenda (Figure 3.2), and to comply with the approach of accountability, tracking of implementation and achievement of the NDCs within the framework of Articles 4 and 13 of the Paris Agreement.

Figure 3.1. Work path for strengthening the NDC on mitigation.

Likewise, the greatest emission reduction opportunities in the short, medium and long term were prioritized; to this end, trend projections to 2035 were made by category and subcategory making up each INGEI sector under two scenarios: the situation with and without the mitigation measure.

This participatory analysis with the interministerial and intersectoral INGEI team made it possible to define as the overall target maintaining a 20% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030, relative to the trend baseline (2024-2030).

Figure 3.2. Main interactions envisaged among the climate change mitigation sectors, planned for implementation within the framework of the Second NDC 2025.

This NDC target of mitigated and avoided emissions was set through an estimate of the GHG emission reduction potential aggregated across sectors, and is associated with a series of measures, lines of action and initiatives, divided into the 5 INGEI sectors: i) Energy; ii) Industrial processes and product use (IPPU); i¡¡) Agriculture; iv) LULUCF; and v) Waste and residues (Figure 3.3), which will be implemented within a framework of shared management and co-responsibility in the implementation of climate action based on a participatory and inclusive process.

Figure 3.3. INGEI sectors.

It is worth highlighting the fundamental role of the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) Sector in achieving the objectives and targets (GHG and Non-GHG) established for climate change mitigation, since it is the only sector capable of capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. According to the results of the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory (INGEI 2024), the LULUCF sector captured -285.198,53 CO2 net in 2022 (Figure 3.4).

These results of the most recent National Greenhouse Gas Inventory Report 1990-2022 have shown that Venezuela is a carbon neutral country. This historic achievement is the result of the ecosocialist policies implemented, which include the sustainable management of 68,4% of our territory under Areas of Special Administration Regime (ABRAE), as well as the implementation of national ecosystem restoration strategies and conservation work promoted within the framework of the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan for the seven great transformations (2025-2031).

All of this is based on a participatory and inclusive interministerial and multisectoral process with People's Power, which will allow the country to advance in complying with the Paris Agreement and fight against the adverse effects of the global environmental crisis affecting us, as well as achieve the target of a 20% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030.

Figure 3.4. Overall INGEI results of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, year 2022.

These ecosystem-based climate mitigation actions of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, with a gender, generational, worldview and intercultural approach, are part of the cross-cutting elements that contribute both to reducing GHG emissions and to the establishment and permanence of carbon reservoirs in ecosystems and agroecosystems, as well as to adaptation to climate change.

This fact makes Venezuela Carbon Neutral; therefore, in this Second Nationally Determined Contribution, the LULUCF sector represents a key factor in national efforts, under the motto of the leader of the Bolivarian Revolution, Hugo Chávez Frías, “let's not change the climate, let's change the system” (COP 15, 2009), which are strengthened in the seven vertices or lines of action of the Gran Misión Madre Tierra Venezuela.

Likewise, in accordance with the Paris Agreement, the Sustainable Development Goals and the political commitment framed in the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan for the 7 great transformations (2025-2031), in the nation's fifth historic objective “Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species”, in the sixth transformation “Ecosocialism” and the fourth vertex or line of action “Climate for life” of the Gran Misión Madre Tierra.

This demonstrates the high political commitment of the Venezuelan State within the framework of the Paris Agreement, adopted through decision 1/CP.21.

M1. NATIONAL CLIMATE CHANGE INFORMATION SYSTEM (SINAICC)

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Implement a National Climate Change Information System to contribute to the management of public policies through the collection, measurement, monitoring, evaluation and reporting of adaptation, mitigation, climate finance and loss and damage measures, enabling the reporting of progress on the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory and all information that feeds into the preparation of the Biennial Transparency Report (BTR) of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

General description

The National Climate Change Information System (SINAICC) will establish mechanisms for collecting information on the indicators planned and determined at the national level in the components of Adaptation, Mitigation and Loss and Damage from climate change, which will enable monitoring, tracking, evaluation, quality control and quality assurance of climate change documentation of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. This will help comply with the reports linked to International Agreements on climate change.

Its design and implementation are adapted to the legal and institutional framework in order to continue improving existing arrangements, under which national commitments and actions have been measured, reported and verified (MVR) under the guidelines of the Presidential Commission for Climate Change.

The System will establish the mandatory information requirements for greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories and the information needed to track progress in implementing and achieving the NDC, assigning the responsibilities of all parties involved at the national level and ensuring the flow of information for the effective achievement of the objectives agreed under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Enhanced Transparency Framework provided for in article 13 of the Paris Agreement.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

It is linked to the reporting of the GHG gases of each sector.

Line of action or initiatives
  • Develop a technological platform, suited to the national regulatory context and to the international protocols of transparency, commitment and co-responsibility established in the Paris Agreement (AP) and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
  • Identify the actors of all programs, projects and actions that fall within the NDCs, and the actions carried out in the adaptation, mitigation, and loss and damage components.
  • Establish reliable and verifiable mechanisms for collection, measurement, reporting and verification (MVR), and monitoring and evaluation (M&E) as established in the general and specific provisions and procedures set out in the modalities, procedures and guidelines (MPGs) and in decisions 1/CP.21, 4/CMA.l, 5/CMA.3, 9/CMA.l and 18/CMA.l, which strengthens the mechanisms for monitoring, evaluating and tracking the progress made in formulation and progress tracking
  • Monitor the impacts and reach of public management, for the implementation of continuous improvements in the incorporation of new adaptation, mitigation and loss and damage measures that contribute to the NDCs, plans, programs and projects.

Type of instrument

Territorial, Operational and Regulatory.

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Homeland Plan 2019-2025

Historic Objective No. 5. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25.

Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology

Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism.

SDG 17: Partnerships for the goals.

II. Linked measures and actions for meeting the sectoral NDC

No.

Name of the Measure and actions

Specific objective

Scope

Mitigation co-benefits according to the mitigation measure or action

Challenges and barriers to implementing measures

Measure No. 1

Design and launch of module I “Adaptation”.

Record and measure the impact of climate change adaptation actions, based on SMART indicators.

This module includes four (04) submodules that will make it possible to determine:

  • The vulnerability assessment.
  • The tracking of the NDCs on adaptation.
  • The tracking of the National Adaptation Plan.
  • Promotion of awareness-raising and citizen participation.

Establish the country's adaptation efforts, in accordance with the measures and actions established by the sectors involved in the Nationally Determined Contribution.

Involvement of the actors in the design and implementation of each of the phases, modules and submodules that make up the System.

Access to external financing that ensures the availability of resources to guarantee the required technological equipment, as well as the strengthening of the capacities of the personnel who will be responsible for managing the SINAICC.

Measure No. 2

Design and launch of module II “Mitigation”.

Record and measure efforts in the mitigation of greenhouse gases (GHG), so that the INGEI, the NDC and the country's climate policies are tracked transparently.

This module includes four (04) submodules for:

  • The implementation of submodules for GHG inventories.
  • The Tracking of the NDCs in terms of mitigation.
  • Measurement of the National Mitigation Plan and NAMAs.

The launch of this module will provide a robust system for monitoring, verification and comprehensive review of the measures adopted on mitigation, enabling decision-making in the accountability process established by the Paris Agreement.

Measure No. 3

Design and launch of module III “Loss and damage”.

Measure the country's risks and vulnerability to climate change, as well as the loss and damage caused by climate change in the territory.

This module comprises five (05) submodules that will enable the recording of both economic and non-economic damage, providing indicators to measure impacts on infrastructure, tourism, agricultural production, biodiversity, ecosystems and human life.

The implementation of this module will help generate timely mechanisms that make it possible to generate actions such as early measures and responses to events.

Measure No. 4

Design and launch of module IV “Financing”

Consolidate a database recording the country's climate finance requested and received (national and international funds.

This module is vital to guarantee transparency and the tracking of the resources allocated to climate action; it will have three (03) submodules.

Effective development of the control of resources to ensure accountability, in accordance with the principles established in the Paris Agreement: completeness, transparency, avoidance of double counting, accuracy, comparability, consistency, and environmental integrity.

M2. PROMOTION OF ENERGY EFFICIENCY AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Promote energy efficiency at the national level, in order to contribute to the reduction of 20% of the country's GHG emissions during the period 2025-2030.

General description

Within the framework of the policies of the Venezuelan State to contribute to the fulfillment of the targets and the SDGs, the Ministry of People's Power for Electric Energy implements the National Energy Efficiency Plan (PNEE), which is carried out by the Vice Ministry of New Sources and Rational and Efficient Use of Electric Energy (DGUREE), through the General Directorate of Rational and Efficient Use of Electric Energy, to contribute to reducing electricity consumption, advance toward a new culture of energy efficiency and strengthen the national electricity system, with the aim of addressing the challenges of climate change and the development of the human city for good living, improving public services and national infrastructure.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

The action is directed at the entire national territory.

Gases (GHG)

1. Carbon Dioxide (CO2) 2. Methane (CH4) 3. Nitrous Oxide (N2O)

Line of action or initiatives
  • Implement plans for the rational and efficient use of energy in large public and private users.
  • Program of Standardization and Technical Regulations for Energy Efficiency Labeling.
  • Execution of the Plan for the replacement of public lighting with high energy efficiency equipment at the National level.
  • Promote the construction of energy-efficient buildings.

Type of instrument

Regulatory/operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations (2025-2031)

STRATEGIC DRIVING LINE: Strengthen the national electricity system as support for the energy matrix oriented to national productive activity.

FOCUS OF ACTION:

Ensure the reliability of the National Electricity System through the strengthening and expansion of electricity generation, transmission, distribution, commercialization and dispatch systems.

Expansion of the electricity system in response to the demands of productive expansion. Generate public policies for the design and management of the National Electricity System, which takes on the national energy matrix in accordance with the expansion demands of the productive system and the settlement patterns and dynamics of the regional urban system, technologies, training, industrial management and development, investment and maintenance plans, guaranteeing its security, stability and monitoring.

Second Transformation:

Human City for Good Living. Public Services and Infrastructure.

Link to the SDGs

SDG 3: Good health and well-being.

SDG 4: Quality education.

M3. PROMOTION OF ECO-ENERGY MANAGEMENT AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Promote eco-energy management in the electricity sector in order to contribute to the reduction of 20% of the country's GHG emissions during the period 2025-2030.

General description

Within the framework of the policies of the Venezuelan State to contribute to the fulfillment of the targets and the SDGs, the Ministry of People's Power for Electric Energy has undertaken the formulation of the National Plan for Eco-energy Management of the Electricity Sector in the face of the Climate Crisis (PLANEC), which is carried out by the Vice Ministry for New Sources and Rational and Efficient Use of Electric Energy, through the General Directorate of Eco-energy Management (DGGEC), which proposes the development of a Mitigation Program that seeks, as part of the climate actions from the Electricity Sector, to address the challenges of climate change and the development of the human city for good living.

As part of the actions contemplated in the Mitigation Program, the development of the following is proposed:

  • GHG measures:

Implementation of Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (CEMS) for greenhouse gases in power generation plants that consume fossil fuels (diesel and fuel oil), which seeks to reduce the emission of approximately 2.940 Gg COzeq during the period from 2025 to 2030.

  • Non-GHG measures:

Development of an Interactive Climate Action Map of the Electricity Sector, which will make it possible to visualize and manage projects on renewable and alternative energies, as well as energy efficiency, in order to contribute to the reduction of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions.

It also includes the monitoring of the National Alternative Energy Plan (PNEA), the National Energy Education and Efficiency Program (PNEDUCEE), as well as the monitoring of the Electricity Sector Development Plan.

Carbon Dioxide (CO2)

Scope and coverage of the NDC

The action is directed at the entire national territory.

Gases (GHG)

MethaneCCI-L)

Nitrous Oxide (N2O)

Line of action or initiatives

Design the Mitigation Program in order to identify and determine the most viable and highest-impact solutions for reducing Greenhouse Gases in the electricity sector. Implement Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (CEMS) for greenhouse gases in thermoelectric generation plants in order to contribute to climate action from the electricity sector. Develop the Interactive Map of Climate Actions of the National Electricity System, which will make it possible to visualize and manage projects on alternative energies and energy efficiency, as well as the emissions avoided by the implementation of these projects.

Territorial and Operational

M4. DIVERSIFICATION OF THE NATIONAL ELECTRICITY GENERATION MATRIX THROUGH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF RENEWABLE AND ALTERNATIVE ENERGY SYSTEMS

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Diversify the National Energy Matrix with the incorporation of Renewable and Alternative Energy Systems, in order to contribute to the reduction of 20% of the country's GHG emissions during the period 2025-2030.

General description

Within the framework of the policies of the Venezuelan State to contribute to the fulfillment of the targets and the SDGs, the Ministry of People's Power for Electric Energy implements the National Alternative Energy Plan (PNEA), which is carried out by the Vice Ministry for New Sources and Rational and Efficient Use of Electric Energy, through the General Directorate of Alternative Energy (DGEA), which proposes the incorporation of 5.450 MW, based on renewable and alternative energies such as solar, wind, biomass and small hydroelectric plants, to serve prioritized sectors such as: health, education, agri-food, housing, tourism and public services such as mobility, water, electricity, among others. The development of this Plan seeks, as part of the climate actions from the Electricity Sector, to address the challenges of climate change and the development of the human city for good living.

With the installed capacity of 5.450 MW in renewable generation, it is projected to serve the entire national territory, while avoiding the emission of approximately 3.898 Gg CÜ2eq, equivalent to a reduction of 13,3% of the sector's emissions, estimated at 174.161 Gg CCheq, for the period from 2025 to 2030. In addition, it represents savings for the country of 9.907.835 Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE).

The distribution of the target by energy source and type of connection to the National Electricity System (SEN) is presented below:

  • With connection to the SEN: 4.250 MW Solar Parks 3.000 MW Wind Parks 1.000 MW Biomass generation plant (MSW) 250 MW
  • Without connection to the SEN: 800 MW Renewable Energy Systems 300 MW RES at charging stations (Electromobility ) 220 MW Small Hydroelectric Plants 200 MW Solar lighting systems and solar heaters 80 MW
  • Self-generation with RES (solar/wind) large consumers: 400 MW

Additionally, the replacement of liquid fuels (diesel/fuel oil) with natural gas for electricity generation is contemplated in 7 thermal plants: Planta Centro (2.600 MW), Planta Táchira (267 MW), Santa Inés (90 MW), Casigua (77 MW), Rafael Urdaneta (259 MW), Santa Bárbara (44 MW) and Josefa Camejo (450 MW), in order to reduce emissions by 1.795 GgCO2eq, which represents a reduction of 6,20% for the sector.

With these measures, the aim is to contribute the following to the National Electricity System:

  • Increase Energy Efficiency.
  • Increase Stability.
  • Reduce the consumption of fossil fuels.
  • Foster the sustainable development of productive sectors.
  • Contribute from the electricity sector to the reduction of 20% of the country's GHG emissions.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

The action is directed at the entire national territory.

Gases (GHG)
  • Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
  • Methane(CH4)
  • Nitrous Oxide (N2O)

Line of action or initiatives
  • Promote the approval of the Law on Renewable and Alternative Energies (LERA), as a framework to legally and technically regulate the incorporation of alternative energies, prioritizing Solar and Wind sources, for self-generation systems of public and private users of the SEN, and generation with Solar, Wind and Biomass parks that can be incorporated into the SEN.
  • Promote alternative energy generation projects, connected to the electricity grid, isolated from the grid (rural, Indigenous and border communities), as well as self-generation, using technologies that harness solar, wind, biomass and hydro energy sources. Access to clean and affordable energy sources contributes to reducing social inequality and improving the living conditions of vulnerable populations, and considering that women increasingly assume the role of natural leaders in communities, the gender perspective is favored in the Fight against the climate crisis.
  • Promote technological and financial agreements and alliances that contribute to establishing the infrastructure required for these new energies, facilitating linkages and alliances for the creation of factories for equipment and components of alternative energy generation systems.
  • Strengthen the technical training of national personnel in the area of renewable and alternative energies, in the areas of project design, installation, operation and maintenance of alternative generation systems.
  • Promote proposals for the promotion, research and development of Alternative Energy, as well as all those strategies and actions necessary for the development of the National Renewable and Alternative Energy Plan (PNEA 2025-2030).

Regulatory/Operational

M5. NATIONAL STRATEGY TO REDUCE EMISSIONS IN THE OPERATIONAL PROCESSES OF THE AIR TRANSPORT SYSTEM AT THE AIRPORTS ADMINISTERED BY BAER, S.A

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and the carbon footprint of the operations carried out at the Santiago Mariño, La Chinita, José Antonio Anzoátegui, Cipriano Castro, Mayor Buenaventura Vivas Guerrero and Juan Pablo Pérez Alfonzo airports, attached to Bolivariana de Aeropuertos (BAER), S.A, for the period 2025- 20230.

General description

The strategy seeks to reduce GHG emissions and the carbon footprint through a comprehensive approach covering: energy efficiency, waste management and environmental management at the Airports and Aerodromes Administered by Bolivariana de Aeropuertos (BAER), S.A, as well as the collection of statistical information to determine the data needed for calculating emissions, as a representative input for the INGEI.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

5 states of the country. Nueva Esparta, Zulia, Anzoátegui, Táchira, Mérida

Gases (GHG)
  • Methane (CH4)
  • Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
  • Nitrous oxide (N2O)

Line of action or initiatives

Bolivariana de Aeropuertos (BAER), S.A. establishes the following actions as a climate change mitigation measure at the Administered Airports and Aerodromes to contribute to climate change mitigation:

  • Preparation of a statistical register for the measurement of greenhouse gases applying IPCC methodologies. And the determination of the carbon footprint of airports and aerodromes.
  • Monitoring and operational control of energy efficiency.
  • Voluntary airport brigades for climate change awareness.

Type of instrument

Territorial and operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 -2025

Great Historical Objective No. 5: Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

National objective:

5.4. Contribute to the formation of a great global movement to contain the causes and repair the effects of climate change that occur as a consequence of the predatory capitalist model.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25:

Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

6.1. Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism.

6.2 Sustain national and international policies against the climate crisis.

Legal Framework:

The established actions consider the statistical variables contained in international standards and regulations, Document No. 9889 “Airport Air Quality Manual” of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and, at the national level, the Civil Aeronautics Law and the operational technical standards issued by INAC through the Civil Aeronautics Regulation.

M6. NATIONAL STRATEGY FOR THE REDUCTION OF CO2 EMISSIONS IN THE OPERATIONAL PROCESSES OF THE AIR TRANSPORT SYSTEM FROM INTERNATIONAL FLIGHTS

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Monitor CO2 emission levels from international flights operated by aircraft operators (airlines) based in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela for the period 2025-2030.

General description

The measure will make it possible to determine the amount of fuel used and its relationship with the emissions generated by international flights of air operators resident in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

Methane (CH4), Carbon Dioxide (CO2), Nitrous oxide (N2O)

Line of action 0 initiatives

The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) states that passenger traffic in the air sector has increased significantly. To the same extent, high levels of GHG emissions are generated, making it one of the sectors that contribute most to this situation. In this regard, the Venezuelan State, through the governing body with competence in the regulation of civil aeronautics (INAC), adopts as a climate change mitigation measure the control and monitoring of GHG emissions generated by aircraft on international flights, which will make it possible, in the medium term, to adopt better practices with respect to air quality, generate actions that mitigate these emissions, and foster the sustainable development of commercial air transport.

Type of instrument

Regulatory/ Operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Homeland Plan 2019 -2025

Great Historical Objective No. 5: Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

National Objective:

5.4. Contribute to the formation of a great global movement to contain the causes and repair the effects of climate change that occur as a consequence of the predatory capitalist model.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25: Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

6.1. Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism.

6.2 Sustain national and international policies against the climate crisis.

Legal Framework

The established actions consider the statistical variables in Document No. 9889 “Airport Air Quality Manual” of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and, at the national level, the Civil Aeronautics Law and the operational technical standards issued by INAC through the Civil Aeronautics Regulation.

Explanatory Notes:

  • For the design of the baseline, the concept of cumulative total emissions was considered as a reference, specifically the scenario proposed in item 4.3.3 of the ICAO document “Report on the Feasibility of a Long-Term Aspirational Goal (LTAG) for International Civil Aviation CO2 Emissions Reductions” of limiting global warming to 2,0°C with a probability of 67%, for which emissions must not exceed 1.15OGtCO2where emissions from international flights represent 3,9% of from 2020 onward, that is, they do not exceed 44,85GtCÜ2 (referring to 44 million 850 thousand tonnes of CO2).
  • The analysis is carried out not on a specific year but with the concept of total emissions, which is 734.096,9TnCO2 (total period 2019 - 2023) representing 0,01636%, of which an increase of 366,70% is expected (2.691.786,51292TnCO2 equivalent to 0.059988848%) period 2025 - 2030 relative to the period 2019 - 2023.
  • The sectoral target was established considering that total emissions do not exceed 448.631,08548TnCO2 (448,63108548KtCO2) per year during the period 2025 - 2030, which would be equivalent to 61,11% annually of the 366,70% that is estimated could increase during the period 2025 - 2030. However, this increase is within the range to contribute to limiting global warming to 2,0°C as indicated in the first note.
  • Evolution of total CO2 emissions during the period 2019 - 2023 (expressed as year/total emissions TnCO2): 2019 / 236.456TnCO2; 2020 / 95.601,43 TnCO2; 2021 /130.499,47TnCO2; 2022 / 138.520,30TnC02; 2023 /133.019,70TnCO2.
  • To calculate the general sectoral target, the total percentage that is expected not to be exceeded (366,68) was divided by 6 (number of years in the period 2025 - 2030), because 2025 is the year in which reporting begins.
  • Specific calculation note: the formula for calculating CO2emissions is the one set out by ICAO in Annex 16 to the Convention on Civil Aviation entitled “Environmental Protection” Volume IV, described in Chapter 2, pp27. item 2.2.3.3.

Where:

CO2: CO2 emissions (tonnes)

Mf: Mass of fuel f used (in tonnes)

FCFf: fuel conversion factor of the given fuel f, equal to 3,16 (in Kg CO2/Kg of fuel) for Jet A / Jet Al / TS-1 fuel or No. 3 jet fuel and 3,10 (in Kg CO2/Kg of fuel) for AVGAS and Jet B fuel.

M7. REDUCTION OF GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS GENERATED BY GROUND OPERATIONS SUPPORT VEHICLES FOR THE AIRCRAFT OF THE AIRLINE AEROPOSTAL ALAS DE VENEZUELA.

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Replace the gasoline and diesel fuel system of Aeropostal's aircraft ground operations support vehicles with compressed natural gas for vehicles (GNV), to reduce CO2 generation, within a period of five (05) years.

General description

Aeropostal's aircraft ground operations support vehicles, specifically aircraft tugs and electric/pneumatic power unit tugs, baggage conveyor belt trucks, lavatory waste collection tankers, water tankers, catering trucks, worker transport, among others, use gasoline and diesel as fuel, which results in considerable generation of Greenhouse Gases; therefore, conversion to Vehicular Natural Gas (GNV) is required, with high-efficiency 5th-generation equipment, to reduce particulate matter by 99 % and decrease CO2 emissions by 50 %, within a period of five (05) years.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

This measure covers all of Aeropostal's aircraft ground operations support vehicles located at the Maiquetía and Porlamar stations.

(GHG) ' '

CO

Line of action or initiatives
  • Acquire the GNV fuel systems, in agreement with PDVSA.
  • Acquire tools, parts and spare parts, in agreement with PDVSA.
  • Implement a training program for the personnel who will operate the GNV vehicles, in agreement with UNETRANS.
  • Train the personnel who will carry out maintenance (at its different levels) on the GNV vehicles, in agreement with PDVSA S.A and UNETRANS.
  • Establish GNV dispensing stations at the service stations located at the Maiquetía and Porlamar Airports, in agreement with PDVSA.
  • Design a preventive maintenance program.
  • Develop the project for the conversion of the vehicles' fuel system through an agreement with PDVSA S.A and UNETRANS.

M8. MODERNIZATION OF THE OPERATIONAL SYSTEM OF THE AUTONOMOUS INSTITUTE MAIQUETÍA INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES IN AIRPORT OPERATIONS

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Promote efficiency in the lighting, air conditioning, waste and other operational systems used in the air operations carried out at the Maiquetía International Airport Autonomous Institute, in order to reduce GHG emissions by 2030.

General description

Implement projects to reduce emissions equivalent to those generated by the carbon footprint at Maiquetía airport.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

State-level Gases (GHG)

CO2, NOx, CH4

Line of action or initiatives

To achieve the scope of the measure, the following actions are proposed:

  • Modernization of lighting and air-conditioning systems.
  • Promotion of the use of renewable energy sources to supply part of the airport's energy needs.
  • Establishment of a comprehensive solid waste management system that promotes recycling and the reduction of waste generated by airport operations.
  • Implement monitoring stations at strategic points of the airport to continuously measure GHG emissions.

Operational and Regulatory

Measure No. 1

Promotion of energy efficiency in the airport facilities through the modernization of lighting and air-conditioning systems.

Reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, while improving passenger comfort and experience.

Replacement of traditional luminaires with LED technology, which offers greater energy efficiency and a longer service life.

Installation of more efficient HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) systems incorporating automatic controls and sensors to regulate temperature and air quality according to occupancy and external conditions.

Consideration of the installation of solar panels or geothermal systems to complement the airport's energy demand.

Strengthening of staff capacities in sustainable practices and in the efficient use of the new systems.

The reduction in energy consumption translates into significant savings on electricity bills, improving the airport's profitability.

Modern air-conditioning systems can improve air quality, benefiting the health and well-being of both employees and passengers.

The adoption of energy-efficient technologies contributes to global sustainability objectives and can improve the airport's image among stakeholders and the general public.

The strengthening of institutional, technical and technological capacities is required. Receiving support with Financing is key.

Measure No. 2

Promotion of the use of renewable energy sources to supply part of the airport's energy needs.

Diversify the airport's energy matrix, thereby reducing dependence on fossil fuels and decreasing greenhouse gas emissions.

Implementation of solar panels on the roofs of terminals, parking lots and other airport structures.

Self-generation of energy can considerably reduce the airport's operating costs in the long term.

By reducing the airport's carbon footprint, it contributes to the fight against climate change and improves local air quality.

Measure No. 3

Establishment of a comprehensive waste management system that promotes recycling and the reduction of waste generated by airport operations.

Establish a comprehensive waste management system at the airport to minimize waste generation and maximize recycling, promoting sustainable practices that reduce the environmental impact of airport operations.

Carry out a diagnosis to identify the types and volumes of waste generated at the airport and develop the recycling Utilization plan.

The reduction in waste generation can lead to a reduction in the costs associated with waste management and disposal.

The adoption of sustainable practices improves the public perception of the airport, attracting passengers who value commitment to the environment and efforts to address climate change.

Measure No. 4

Establishment of a continuous monitoring system for emissions generated by airport operations, aligned with international standards.

Establishing a continuous monitoring system for emissions generated by airport operations means obtaining precise, real-time data on emissions of greenhouse gases and other pollutants.

Implement monitoring stations at strategic points of the airport to continuously measure emissions of CO2, NOx, CH4, suspended particles and other pollutants.

By identifying and managing emission sources, measures can be implemented that improve air quality in and around the airport, benefiting both workers and passengers.

Real-time data allow airport operators to optimize operations, reducing fuel consumption and, consequently, the associated emissions.

M9. NATIONAL PLAN FOR THE MODERNIZATION AND REHABILITATION OF THE SURFACE TRANSPORT SYSTEM

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Rehabilitate the Surface Transport System, advancing toward greater sustainability, in order to reduce CO2 emissions by 2030, through the public enterprises of the Venezuelan State with competence in providing urban and interurban mobility services.

General description

The transport sector of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela is a vital component for multimodal mobility. The Gran Misión Transporte Venezuela has been fundamental in this process, promoting the rehabilitation and modernization of infrastructure, as well as the integration of a multimodal system that facilitates connectivity between regions. This is an effort by the Venezuelan State despite the challenges it faces due to the negative impact of the Unilateral Coercive Measures on investment and maintenance; the sector strives to improve the quality of service and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, aligning itself with international commitments on sustainability and climate change. In response to this, the country is moving forward in strengthening policies for the recovery, rehabilitation and replacement of the units that make up the surface public transport System and promotes sustainable mobility in cities, fleet renewal under updated regulations, and the acquisition of spare parts, parts and components for major maintenance of units and physical plants; likewise, the sector implements landscaping throughout the installed infrastructure with the aim of achieving sustainable mobility.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National.

Gases (GHG)

CO2

Line of action or initiatives

The initiatives proposed by the Venezuelan State through the companies providing mass mobility services include:

  • Routine, preventive and major and minor corrective maintenance of the units.
  • Implementation of natural gas in transport units to achieve GHG reduction.
  • Renewal of transport unit fleets.
  • Awareness campaigns on the use of passenger transport and sustainable mobility.
  • Arboriculture and urban landscaping campaigns.

Territorial, Operational and Regulatory

M10. STRENGTHENING OF THE NATIONAL METRO AND RAILWAY SYSTEM

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Strengthen, by 2030, the Metro and Railway Transport System as a multimodal mobility mechanism through the public enterprises of the Venezuelan State with competence in providing the service, so as to ensure increased user mobility through this service, thereby helping to avoid the GHG emissions generated as a consequence of the use of surface transport.

General description

Multimodal transport emerges as an effective strategy to reduce CO2 emissions associated with passenger transport, enabling a shift towards more sustainable modes of transport depending on the distance to be travelled from the point of origin to the destination. That is why the Venezuelan State maintains a sustained effort to guarantee a safe multimodal transport service that at the same time contributes to reducing the GHG emissions generated by the surface transport system.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

CO2avoided

Line of action or initiatives

The initiatives proposed by the Venezuelan State through the companies providing rail and metro mass mobility services include:

  • Maintenance of trains and renewal of the existing fleet.
  • Expansion of railway networks
  • Maintenance and renewal of units to improve the service offering
  • Expansion of metro systems.
  • Innovation of the Train Fleet
  • Capacity building for the improvement and modernization of railway and metro systems in the country.

Type of instrument

Territorial, Operational and Regulatory

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 - 2025.

Historical Objective 3: Turn Venezuela into a social, economic and political powerhouse within the great emerging power of Latin America and the Caribbean, guaranteeing the creation of a zone of peace in our America.

National Objective 3.2: Deepen the construction of a New National Geopolitics using as structuring elements systemic, geo-historical and functional regionalization, the regional urban system and infrastructure, services and mobility in the development of the spatial dimension of Socialism.

Strategic Objective 3.2.5. Articulate, maintain and generate a solid, efficient and interconnected national mobility and intermodality system, correlated with the functional dynamics of economic specialization and current and projected flows, the regional urban system, as well as its maintenance, monitoring and management system and its industrial components.

Great Historical Objective No. 5: Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

National Objective 5.4. Contribute to the formation of a great global movement to contain the causes and repair the effects of climate change that occur as a consequence of the predatory capitalist model.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25:

Transport system as a sovereign State public policy. Strengthen and promotethe sectoral transport plan and in particular the articulated mobility system, as a national public policy, governing its different components and scales, in order to optimize the system's efficiency, its monitoring, management and prospective vision according to economic and urban-regional dynamics.

Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism: The right to the city and confronting the climate emergency and defense of the Venezuelan Amazon. 6.1 . Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism. 6.2 Sustain national and international policies against the climate crisis.

Link to the SDGs

SDG 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure.

SDG 13: Climate action.

SDG 17: Partnerships for the goals.

M11. MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT PLAN FOR HEAVY CARGO TRANSPORT UNITS

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Have a modern and environmentally sustainable cargo vehicle fleet, which includes the replacement of the vehicle stock that has reached the end of its operational useful life and the execution of a major, minor, preventive and corrective maintenance plan that guarantees the operability of the fleet of heavy cargo transport units in the country, in order to ensure the progressive and sustained reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, which translates into improved air quality.

General description

Corpologística, as the state heavy cargo transport company, takes actions seeking to mitigate GHG emissions; to this end, as part of the climate action effort, the replacement of units that have reached the end of their useful life is planned, as well as guaranteeing the preventive and corrective maintenance of its vehicle stock.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG) Carbon dioxide (CO2)

Line of action or initiatives

The measure includes:

  • The replacement of public sector cargo transport units that have already reached the end of their useful life and operational capacity.
  • Ensuring the major, minor, preventive and corrective maintenance of the Corporation's cargo transport fleet.

Type of instrument

Territorial - Operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 - 2025. Historical Objective 2: Continue building Bolivarian socialism of the XXI century in Venezuela, as an alternative to the destructive and savage system of capitalism, and thereby ensure “the greatest possible sum of happiness, the greatest sum of social security and the greatest sum of political stability” for our people. National Objective 2.1. Generate the economic and material bases for the humanly gratifying transition towards socialism, transforming the oil rentier culture into an inclusive, efficient and fair productive economic model, liberating the productive forces, in order to satisfy the needs of our population and the powerhouse country. Strategic Objective 2.1.6. Strengthen the system of direct distribution of inputs and products, attacking the speculation inherent to capitalism, to guarantee the satisfaction of the needs of the people. Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25. IT: Economic Transformation, the new National Economic Model Strategic Line of Impetus: Alternative Distribution System Focus of Action: • Re-empowerment of logistics and distribution chains. • Re-empower transport and distribution systems. • Strengthen a critical and strategic roadmap for national cargo transport. 6T: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology. 6.1 . Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism. 6.2 Sustain national and international policies against the climate crisis.

M12. REDUCTION OF GHG EMISSIONS CAUSED BY SHIPS

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Regulate the implementation of policies, programs, plans and projects promoted for the actions of the State through water transport for climate change mitigation.

General description

Guidelines are established for the documentary and physical inspection of ships, in order to supervise, prevent and reduce air pollution produced by emissions of nitrogen oxide (NOx) and sulphur oxide (SOx), in order to reduce GHG emissions in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National (National port system of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela)

Gases (GHG)

Sulphur oxides (SOx) (SOx)

Nitrogen oxides (NOx)

Line of action or initiatives
  • Physical and documentary inspection to review the procedures for verifying gas emissions based on the fuel oil samples stipulated in Annex VI of the MARPOL Convention (Regulation 18.8.2 or Regulation 14.8).
  • Control in relation to nitrous oxides (NOx).
  • Control of sulphur oxide (SOx) emissions.
  • Control of volatile organic compounds (VOC).

Type of instrument

Territorial and Regulatory: INEA Administrative Order No. 056. 08 July 2024. Resolution MEPC.328(76), MARPOL Annex VI.

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 - 2025.

Great historical objective V. Contribute to the preservation of life on the Planet and the salvation of the human species.

5.4. Contribute to the formation of a great global movement to contain the causes and repair the effects of climate change that occur as a consequence of the predatory capitalist model

5.2. 1.2.2. Promote clean industrial technologies that guarantee effluents and emissions with less need for treatment for their purity.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25.

ecosocialism. Focus of action: Modernization and environmental monitoring system.
