M13. AIR AND WATER QUALITY MONITORING IN MARINE ENVIRONMENTS

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Monitor air and water quality in the areas of influence of the Los Roques and Los Monjes archipelagos, and the pier of the Juan Crisóstomo Falcón Naval Base located on the Paraguaná peninsula, Falcón state.

General description

Point sampling of Total Suspended Particles (TSP), PM10, PM2,5 in the atmosphere, and of NO2 and SÜ2gases will be carried out in the areas of influence of the Los Roques and Los Monjes archipelagos, and the dock of the Juan Crisóstomo Falcón Naval Base located on the Paraguaná peninsula, Falcón state.

M14. PILOT MONITORING OF BLUE CARBON ASSOCIATED WITH SEAGRASS MEADOWS IN THE INSULAR AND COASTAL TERRITORY OF VENEZUELA

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Monitor the blue carbon associated with seagrass meadows in the Insular and Coastal Territory of Venezuela, sequestered and stored in the soil and biomass of mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass meadows (PPM) at different sites of the Archipiélago Los Roques National Park (PN), Morrocoy and Laguna de Cocinetas.

General description

Preliminary determination of blue carbon in seagrass systems at different sites in Archipiélago Los Roques NP, Morrocoy NP and Laguna de Cocinetas, through the estimation of soil organic carbon (%Corg) in sediments and existing biomass.

Apply methodologies for the indirect analysis of Corg (%LOI), which include systematic sediment sampling along a 50 m transect, allowing the estimation of vegetation cover using quadrats (0,25m ) and total biomass through sediment core analysis.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

Local. Different sites of Archipiélago Los Roques National Park, Morrocoy NP and Laguna Gases (GHG) de Cocinetas.

CO e 2ec*

Line of action or initiatives

Monitoring and assessment of blue carbon sinks stored in the soil and biomass of mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass meadows.

M15. SPECIAL ENVIRONMENTAL REMEDIATION PLANS

I. Policies, measures and actions.

Objective

Minimize the environmental impact of mining activities, maximize the remediation of environmental liabilities, prioritizing the development and use of low-impact technologies, and e valuating the load on the matrix of energy and natural resources when planning new projects.

General description

The areas that were historically degraded by illegal mining currently form part of a program that is being implemented with each actor in the mineral pro- cessing industrial sector; these special environmental remediation plans constitute added value and a contribution to the community and the environment. In addition, the following activities are added to this:

Creation of agro-mining schools in the various mining areas of Bolívar state: for training volunteer groups from mining communities in environmental conservation and the implementation of mitigation and recovery actions in areas affected by extractive activity.

Creation of nurseries and seedbeds and identification and management of native species: for forest reforestation and environmental recovery of soils in areas where mining activity takes place or those that were historically degraded and maintain this status.

Formation of Ecosocialist Councils in each Communal Circuit: these are socio-productive units that involve the actors of mining activity together with the community and MISION PIAR for the promotion, strengthening, guidance and execution of reforestation and remediation plans in areas affected by mining.

Execution of Audits and Inspections: Through the National Mining Audit and Inspection Service (SENAFIM) and the Vice Ministry for Monitoring and Control of Eco-mining Development, by way of the General Directorate of Ecosocialist Management of Mining Development and the General Directorate of Mining Safeguarding, maintain permanent verification of mining projects in their execution phase, to control and supervise the exploration and exploitation phases, as well as the related processing activities, so that they adhere to the socio-environmental impact studies duly approved by the Ministry of People's Power for Ecosocialism.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

Bolívar, Táchira and Zulia states.

Gases (GHG)

Carbon Dioxide (CO2)

Line of action or initiatives
  • Planting of forest species in areas affected by mining.
  • Selection of projects for the remediation of hectares affected by mining.
  • Implementation of responsible practices and clean technologies in mineral extraction.
  • Development of a capacity-building program for GHG estimation in the mining sector.

Type of instrument

Territorial and operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

The National Executive designed the Homeland Plan 2019 - 2025 and the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, defining as the 5th Historical Objective: “Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species”; this constitutes the execution milestone in terms of short-, medium- and long-term planning and development of the sectoral plans established for each productive sector of Venezuela.

In particular, in the case of the Mining Sector, the Mining Sectoral Plan 2019-2025 was approved, from which derive the remaining specific plans that set out the roadmap for mining activities in a scientific and rational manner, seeking the optimal recovery 0 extraction of the mining resource, in accordance with the principle of sustainable development, favouring environmental con- servation and land-use planning, conceiving ecological and effective mining management.

M16. PROJECTS TO MINIMIZE EMISSIONS FROM NATURAL GAS FLARING AND VENTING

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Execute projects that allow the reduction of emissions from natural gas flaring and venting by 71% during the period(2025-2030), that is 917 MMPCED (□ 20.729 Kt CO2 eq/year) of the total Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions reported by the gas industry in the base year 2024 in the states of Anzoátegui and Monagas, by increasing the capacities for handling, compression, treatment, transport and distribution of the gaseous hydrocarbon intended for consumption by the oil industry and for the national market for the integral industrial development of the country and the social well-being of Venezuela.

General description

The measure includes the minimization of natural gas flaring and venting in the states of Anzoátegui and Monagas; to this end it will be necessary to give continuity to projects associated with the efficiency and energy use of the natural gas generated in oil production activities.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

  • Execution of efficiency and energy use projects.

Industrial Processes and Product Use Sector

M17. NATIONAL PLAN FOR THE PHASE-OUT OF THE CONSUMPTION OF OZONE-DEPLETING SUBSTANCES (SAO) AND PHASE-DOWN OF THE CONSUMPTION OF SUBSTANCES WITH GLOBAL WARMING POTENTIAL (HFC)

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

1. Phase out 67,5% of SAO consumption in the refrigeration and air-conditioning industry relative to the base year by the year 2030 (equivalent to 67,26 TPAO of other ozone-depleting substances. 2. Phase out 67,5% of SAO (R-22) consumption in the refrigeration and air-conditioning industry relative to the base year by the year 2030, which translates into 39,99 TPAO of R-22. 3. Keep HFC consumption equal to or less than 5.157.618,44 TCO2 eq in the period 2025-2028.

General description

Promote the use of more efficient and environmentally friendly refrigeration and air-conditioning technologies that use refrigerants with zero ozone depletion potential and low 0 zero global warming potential.

- Advance in the phase-out of the consumption of ozone-depleting substances (SAO) and the phase-down of the consumption of substances with global warming potential (HFC).

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

SAO gases: R-141: PAO: 0,07/PCA:725; R-141b: PAO: 0,ll/PCA:725; R-142: PAO: 0,07/PCA:2310; R142b: PAO: 0,065/PCA:2310; R-22: PAO: 0,055/PCA:1810; R-123: PAO: 0,02/PCA:77 HFC gases: R-134a: PCA: 1530; R-32: PCA: 771; R-152a: PCA: 124; R-407C: PCA: 1773,85; R-404A: PCA: 3921,6; R-410A: PCA: 2087,5; R-417A: PCA: 2346; R422D: PCA: 2728,95; R-426A: PCA: 1508,4; R-437A: PCA: 1805,05; R-507A: PCA: 3985

Notal: PAO is an abbreviation for ozone depletion potential, (an indicator that measures the degree of degradation that the substance can cause to the ozone layer, compared with the refrigerant gas R-ll, whose PAO is 1 as established by the secretariat). Note 2: PCA is an abbreviation for global warming potential, which indicates the impact a gas has on global warming. It is compared with carbon dioxide (CO2), which has a PCA of 1. Note 3: These gases are according to the behaviour of the latest customs clearances, which does not preclude the gases from changing according to the list established in resolution 227 dated 01/0/2015, Resolution No. 036 dated 12/06/2023 and Decree No.4.335 dated 07/03/2006.

Line of action or initiatives

Lines of action established in the National Plan for the Elimination of SAO Substances for the 2021 NDC that will be maintained in the 2nd NDC 2025, and new lines of action:

  • Support and technical assistance to strengthen the legal framework related to refrigerant gases (HCFC, HFC, HC, HFO), Support and technical assistance to strengthen the technical framework (COVENIN) related to refrigerant gases (HCFC, HFC, HC, HFO), Updating of training material on good refrigeration practices to address three levels of training, basic, intermediate and advanced, according to the technician's level of training, Dissemination of didactic material for games, and informative and educational material on the safe handling of refrigerant gases, Promote the Zero Leaks Program in the hospital, food preservation and private service company sectors, Awareness campaign for the promotion of eco-energy technologies with low global warming potential, Promotion of industrial and technological conversion in the country, Automation of the Licensing System for the import of refrigerant gases (HCFC and HFC), Training for the Ecosocialist Territorial Units (UTEC) and the National Integrated Customs and Tax Administration Service, regarding the safe handling of refrigerant gases, detection of illicit activities, and the national and international legal framework, Annual report to the Montreal Protocol Secretariat on the country's consumption of refrigerant gases for the previous fiscal year, Annual report on the activities carried out within the framework of compliance with the Montreal Protocol and its amendments in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, Training for companies handling refrigerant gases for their safe handling, Request, review and permanent updating of the manuals submitted by importing companies for the safe handling of SAO and HFC refrigerant gases, Technical inspections of companies handling and generating SAO, Meetings and working groups under the subcommittee on Ozone-Depleting Substances and Global Warming Potential belonging to the Presidential Commission on Chemical Safety for the evaluation and discussion of issues inherent to the Montreal Protocol and its Amendments (Energy efficiency, substitution technologies, Tariff codes, industrial conversion), Permanent inspections through the Ecosocialist Territorial Units (UTEC) to check equipment with possible leaks in refrigeration, climate control and air-conditioning equipment.

Territorial and Operational

The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, under the Montreal Protocol, must phase out 67,5% in the case of SAO and have a freeze in the case of HFC, following the 2013-2040 phase-out schedule for SAO and the 2024-2045 phase-down schedule for HFC.

Both the Protocol and its amendments establish the phase-out and phase-down schedules to which ratifying countries are subject; Decision XIX/6 presents the guidelines for the phase-out schedules of ozone-depleting substances, which must be adjusted to each country, and Article 5 of the Kigali Amendment is the item that establishes the schedules and percentages for the phase-down of HFC.

II.1 Estimation of mitigation potential

Code No.

Name of the Measure and actions

Measure application scenario

Without measure

With measure

Measure No. 1

Phase-out of the ozone-depleting substances R-141, R-141b, R-142, R142b and R-123.

Failing to act to progressively phase out ozone-depleting substances would have serious consequences for climate change and the environment:

Increase in ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

Without this protection, there would be an increase in the incidence of skin cancer, cataracts and other health problems in humans, as well as damage to marine and terrestrial ecosystems.

Not eliminating them would contribute significantly to global warming, exacerbating extreme weather events.

Additional UV radiation can negatively affect living organisms, including phytoplankton, which is the base of the marine food chain.

Increased exposure to UV radiation can reduce crop productivity, affecting food security.

Reduction of SAO consumption by 67,5% in the refrigeration and air-conditioning industry by 2030, which translates into 67,26 TPAO of other SAO.

Acting to progressively phase out ozone-depleting substances would have several positive impacts on climate change and the environment:

1. Restoration of the ozone layer.

2. Reduction of global warming.

3. Protection of biodiversity: By reducing UV radiation and global warming, natural habitats and species at risk of extinction would be protected.

4. Improvement of food security. More stable climatic conditions and lower exposure to UV radiation can increase agricultural productivity, ensuring a more reliable food supply and supporting the agricultural economy.

Measure No. 2

Phase-out of the ozone-depleting substance R-22.

Failing to take measures to eliminate R-22 would not only affect human health and biodiversity, but would also accelerate climate change and its devastating effects.

Reduce SAO consumption in the refrigeration and air-conditioning industry by 67,5% by the year 2030, which translates into 39,99 TPAO of R-22.

Acting to progressively phase out the substance R-22, which depletes the ozone layer, would have several positive impacts on climate change and the environment.

1. Reduction of ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

2. Mitigation of global warming.

3. Protection of biodiversity

4. Improvement of food security: More stable climatic conditions and lower exposure to UV radiation can increase agricultural productivity.

5. Mitigating climate change and restoring the ozone layer can reduce the costs associated with natural disasters, improve productivity and avoid the expenses of adapting to new climatic conditions, resulting in long-term economic benefits.

Measure No. 3

Progressive reduction of substances with atmospheric warming potential R-134a, R-32, R-152a, R-407C, R-404A, R-410A, R- 417A, R422D, R-426A, R-437A, R-507A.

Note: These gases are based on the behavior of the latest nationalizations, which does not preclude the gases from changing in accordance with the list established in Resolution No. 227 dated 01/0/2015, Resolution No. 036 dated 12/06/2023 and Decree No. 4.335 dated 07/03/2006.

Failing to take measures to reduce substances with atmospheric warming potential would not only accelerate climate change, but would also have devastating effects on human health, biodiversity and the economy

Keep HFC consumption equal to or less than 5.157.618,44 TCCh eq in the period 2025-2028.

Acting to reduce substances with atmospheric warming potential would not only help curb climate change, but would also have significant benefits for human health, biodiversity and the economy.

Measure No. 4

Acquisition of one (01) refrigerant gas analyser, one (01) leak detector, one (01) gas recovery unit, and one (01) refrigerant gas regenerator to carry out activities inherent to compliance with the Montreal Protocol and its amendments, regarding refrigerant gases seized due to illicit trafficking and incorporated into public sectors of the State.

If the actions are not implemented, it will not be possible to:

1. Train all technical staff of the General Directorate of Environmental Quality Management, the Territorial Units and the National Integrated Service of Customs and Tax Administration (SENIAT).

2. Carry out, nationwide, all verification inspections of companies that import, handle and generate refrigerant gases.

3. Comply with the commitments made by Venezuela under the Montreal Protocol regarding capacity building.

1. Establish a recovery and regeneration center for refrigerant gases seized due to illicit trafficking; once regenerated, they can be incorporated into public sectors of the State, which will also help reduce indirect emissions of refrigerant gases from their production.

2. Plan and carry out a schedule of verification inspections of refrigerant gas handling and possible leaks from climate-control, air-conditioning and refrigeration systems.

3. Trained technical staff.

Measure No. 5

Strengthening of the technical capacities of the staff of the General Directorate of Environmental Quality Management, the Ecosocialist Territorial Units and the National Integrated Customs and Tax Administration Service (SENIAT) regarding the safe handling of refrigerant gases, international agreements and the national legal framework.

Measure No. 6

Execution of technical inspections of companies importing and handling refrigerant gases to verify the handling of these gases, as well as of generating companies to verify the functionality of equipment, avoiding possible leaks.

M18. STRENGTHENING OF THE NATIONAL AIR QUALITY NETWORK

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Strengthen the air quality network in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela in order to achieve an automated monitoring system for atmospheric emissions throughout the national territory, which makes it possible to generate statistical data for consolidating policies, plans and programs aimed at improving air quality and the health of the population. It will also make it possible to apply improvements to the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory (INGEI).

General description
  • Update of the Law on Water and Air Quality and Decree No. 638 Standards on air quality and control of atmospheric pollution.
  • Acquisition and installation of forty-eight (48) Air Quality Monitoring devices for the assessment of chemical parameters associated with atmospheric pollution resulting from industrial and automotive sector activities throughout the national territory, in the period 2025 to 2030.
  • Installation of Air Quality Monitoring devices for the assessment of chemical parameters associated with atmospheric pollution resulting from industrial and automotive sector activities.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs), Tropospheric Ozone (O3), Carbon Monoxide (CO), Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2), Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), Particulates.

Line of action or initiatives

Modernization and environmental monitoring system.

The Venezuelan State has the obligation, with the active participation of society, to guarantee that the population lives in a pollution-free environment, where air, water (...) are especially protected, in accordance with the law, and likewise to reduce and control emissions into the atmosphere produced by the operation of polluting sources, so as to ensure air quality and the well-being of the population and other living beings, in line with the parameters established in the regulations governing them and in compliance with the international agreements signed and ratified by the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

Type of instrument

Territorial, Operational and Regulatory

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 - 2025.

M19. REGULATORY STRENGTHENING IN FAVOR OF SUSTAINABLE AGROECOSYSTEMS

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Apply nature-based mitigation measures through the formulation of legal tools that help minimize the toxic load of the soil and improve human health and agroecosystems. This measure will also make it possible to increase the adaptive capacity of agricultural practices.

General description

Drafting of three (3) proposed legal instruments to implement actions regulating agroecological crop production in order to reduce the toxic load and minimize the impacts of climate change, as well as to regulate or prohibit the agricultural and livestock use of highly and moderately toxic synthetic pesticides.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National: By 2030, three (3) proposed legal instruments will be drafted to implement actions regulating agroecological crop production in order to reduce the toxic load and minimize the impacts of climate change, as well as to regulate or prohibit the agricultural use of highly and moderately toxic synthetic pesticides

Gases (GHG)

Regulatory instrument for comprehensive agricultural health that will progressively contribute to reducing emissions kt CO2 eq

Line of action or initiatives

Promotion of agroecology nationwide based on the principles of ancestral knowledge and respect for the environment. Conservation and preservation of all natural components of sustainable agroecosystems at any scale or dimension. Environmental protection through comprehensive agricultural health. Adopt measures to control, through comprehensive agricultural health, the presence of synthetic chemical contents that affect the quality of soil, air, water, the environment and human health.

Type of instrument

Regulatory

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25.

Measure No. 1

Proposed legal instruments Environmental protection through comprehensive agricultural health

If not implemented, it could cause negative impacts in the country:

1. Soil Degradation. The intensive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides can deplete soil nutrients, reduce its fertility and increase erosion.

2. Loss of Biodiversity: Unsustainable agriculture can lead to the loss of plant and animal species, which reduces ecosystem resilience to pests and diseases.

3. Water Pollution

4. Greenhouse gas emissions may increase, contributing to climate change.

5. It may lead to a decrease in agricultural productivity, putting food security at risk.

6. Impact on the Health of farmers and nearby communities.

Sustainable agricultural soils can act as carbon sinks, capturing and storing carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere. This helps reduce the concentration of greenhouse gases.

Sustainable agricultural practices, such as agroecology, minimize the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, which are significant sources of greenhouse gas emissions.

It improves the resilience of agroecosystems to extreme weather events and diseases, reducing the need for intensive chemical and mechanical interventions.

It ensures a more efficient nutrient cycle, reducing dependence on external inputs and improving soil health in the long term.

It ensures productivity and environmental health in the long term.

M20. STRENGTHENING OF THE NATIONAL SYSTEM OF AREAS UNDER SPECIAL ADMINISTRATION REGIME (ABRAE)

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Continue strengthening the National System of Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE), considering gender perspectives and climate change mitigation strategies

General description

The Venezuelan State has established a National System of Areas Under Special Administration Regime-ABRAE (protected areas) to preserve the ecological heritage, and it continues to be strengthened with policies, plans and programs as a strategic action for land-use planning and sustainable management, the conservation of biological diversity and carbon sinks, and the provision of ecosystem services, in order to generate socio-environmental benefits.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National. It will focus on the regulatory strengthening of 10.464.227,88 hectares distributed across 22 ABRAE, for the conservation of the country's carbon sinks. Regional. It will focus on improving the management of 18.263.462,53 hectares located in 19 ABRAE in Amazonas state and Bolívar state (Caroní River Basin), to improve avoided GHG emissions, conserve carbon sinks and contribute to the conservation of the Venezuelan Guayana and the Amazon Basin.

Gases (GHG)

Conservation of carbon sinks and avoided GHG emissions.

Line of action or initiatives
  • Participatory land-use planning and management of protected areas with a gender, generational, worldview and intercultural approach.
  • Strengthening of the normative and regulatory framework of the national system of protected areas (Areas Under Special Administration Regime-ABRAE).
  • Conservation of forest heritage as a carbon sink.
  • Promotion of low-emission and resilient livelihoods, sustainable production and food security, considering governance frameworks and planning with indigenous communities with a gender, generational, worldview and intercultural approach.

Amazonas state is a highly biodiverse territory, with a great variety of ecosystems that provide multiple ecosystem services; it is important for water resources and plays a role in climate regulation and the capture of greenhouse gases. The Caroní River basin constitutes an area of national and global importance, mostly protected under Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE), with high biological diversity, strategic production of water and clean hydroelectric energy (it provides about 70% of the country's hydroelectric energy), mineral wealth and the presence of ancestral indigenous peoples with their traditions and ways of life.

  • Strengthen capacities to support the effective management and governance of the existing ABRAE within Amazonas state and the Caroní River basin in Bolívar state.

Type of instrument

Territorial, Regulatory and land-use planning for its proper administration and integrated landscape management

Link to Venezuelan State policies

The Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela attaches high importance to development compatible with environmental protection, as expressed in the objectives of the Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019-2025, which establishes in its Objective 5.1. Build and promote the ecosocialist historical social model, based on respect for the rights of Mother Earth and the living well of our people, aimed at the rational, optimal and sustainable use of natural resources, respecting the processes and cycles of nature. 5.2. Protect and defend the permanent sovereignty of the State over its natural heritage and wealth, for the supreme benefit of our People, who will be its main guarantor, as well as a contribution to life on the planet.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907,24/05/25.

  • Fifth Historical Objective. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.
  • Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

6.1. Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism. These NDC measures and actions are also framed within the National Strategy for the Conservation of Biological Diversity 2024-2030. Kunming-Montreal action targets for 2030: Target 2: Ensure that by 2030 at least 30% of areas of degraded terrestrial ecosystems are under effective restoration, in order to enhance biological diversity and ecosystem functions and services, ecological integrity and connectivity. Target 10: Ensure that areas under agriculture, aquaculture, fisheries and forestry are managed sustainably. Target 11: Restore, maintain and enhance nature's contributions to people, including ecosystem functions and services, such as regulation of air, water and climate, soil health, pollination and reduction of disease risk, as well as protection from natural hazards and disasters, through nature-based solutions and ecosystem-based approaches for the benefit of all people and nature. This NDC also contributes to the country's voluntary targets for the National Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) Strategy by 2030, which include increasing forest cover by 262.361 ha, reducing the incidence of forest fires by 50% and the natural regeneration of shrubland and grassland cover as forests

Measure No. 1

Land-Use Plans and Use Regulations (PORU) of the prioritized ABRAE in Amazonas State.

MINEC-GCP/VEN/11199/GFF

Conserve the Venezuelan Amazon forest through the promotion of sustainable, low-emission and resilient livelihoods and production, considering governance and planning frameworks with communities with a gender approach.

Strengthen protected area management through participatory schemes in primary forest and savanna landscapes of high conservation value.

The intervention of the measure will cover Fourteen (14) Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE) of Amazonas state (10.538.305,98 hectares of protected terrestrial areas without considering the overlap between them), which will have Land-Use Plans and Use Regulations (PORU) drafted and socialized. The priority areas identified are:

  • Cataniapo River Watershed Protection Zone: 152.839,1 ha, which includes the Piedra Pintada NM.
  • Alto Orinoco-Casiquiare Biosphere Reserve: 7.725.156,55 ha. This reserve contains the national parks (NP) Parima Tapirapecó, Sierra de la Neblina and part of Duida Marahuaca (203.718,32 ha), as well as the natural monuments (NM) Cerro Vinilla and Cerro Aratitiyope, Sierra Unturán and Cerro Tamacuari, and Serranía Tapirapecó.
  • Sipapo Forest Reserve (FR): 1.541.517,9 ha. It includes the Cerro Autana NM and part of the Macizo Cuao - Sipapo and Cerro Moriche NM (640.853,40 ha).
  • Yapacana National Park: 272.791,26 ha.
  • Piedra La Tortuga Natural Monument: 468,55 ha.

It will make it possible to strengthen management capacities, prioritizing protected areas for conservation and sustainable forest management in decreed ABRAE and other territories of Amazonas state. This will generate guidelines for the conservation and sustainable use of forests that improve the livelihoods of indigenous communities, considering gender perspectives and climate change mitigation strategies, as well as financial sustainability strategies that help strengthen ABRAE management.

State institutions and indigenous communities show willingness to jointly define and implement land-use planning with a focus on integrated landscape management.

Generate outreach processes with indigenous peoples and communities of the Amazon that integrate related topics on the importance of ABRAE, and notions linked to the specific sociocultural and spiritual practices of the territories.

Improve capacities for the sustainable and integrated management of multiple-use landscapes and for governance in the ABRAE, with a gender, generational and intercultural approach.

The intervention of the measure will cover Five (5) Land-Use Plans and Use Regulations (PORU) formulated in a participatory and consensual manner: Canaima National Park, Cadena de Tepuyes National Monuments, La Paragua Forest Reserve, Ikabarú Hydraulic Reserve, Southern Bolívar State Protected Zone.

7.712.919 hectares under improved management for their conservation and sustainable use.

Formulating the ABRAE land-use plans (PORU), through a collaborative approach among the actors involved, will reconfirm a shift from the current emphasis of territorial planning to a holistic approach to landscape management, including the areas of biological diversity conservation, climate change, carbon flows and stocks, water management, ecosystem goods and services, and sustainable livelihood management, including community participation in the benefits.

General description

It is a broad, holistic or fully unified approach to addressing fire-related issues, considering biological, environmental, cultural, social, economic and political interactions, and assuming that fire can generate positive and negative effects for ecosystem conservation for sustainable development. Integrated fire management considers fire management, fire ecology and fire culture as a climate change mitigation measure, “reduction of emissions from biomass burning”.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

Local (Communities of Santa Cruz de Mapauri (Pemón Sector 5, Canaima National Park), Maurak and San Antonio del Morichal (Pemón Sector 6, Santa Elena de Uiaren), forest, moriche palm swamp and savanna ecosystems. Caroní River basin (Bolívar state) and communities of Amazonas state.

Gases (GHG)

CO2

Line of action or initiatives
  • Formation and training of three (03) indigenous community volunteer brigades coordinated with MINEC and INPARQUES and other State entities with local and national competence.
  • Strengthening of indigenous community capacities in integrated fire management.
  • Passive restoration of savanna, forest and moriche palm swamp ecosystems, through the control of forest fires as one of the stressors that prevents the natural recovery of these ecosystems.
  • Geospatial Monitoring and Evaluation System for sustainable and integrated landscape management with emphasis on the study of fires (before, during and after) and the estimation of GHG applying IPCC methodology, for the forest, moriche palm swamp and savanna ecosystems of the Caroní River basin.

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Measure No. 1

Integrated fire management program in the Caroní River basin (Bolívar State). MINEC- GCP/VEN/023/GFF

Strengthen indigenous community capacities in integrated fire management in the Caroní River basin in order to address the ecological, social and technical aspects of fire in an integrated manner, and combat biomass fires.

1. Training for fire management, control and suppression, and formation and equipping of indigenous community brigades.

2. Passive restoration in historically burned areas in forest and savanna ecosystems.

A minimum area of protection against forest fires is delimited in the Caroní River basin of 12.081 hectares of savanna, 300 of forest and 328 of moriche palm swamps, and, in Amazonas state, of 300 hectares of forest, for the passive restoration of these ecosystems.

3. Geospatial Monitoring and Evaluation System for sustainable and integrated landscape management with emphasis on the study of fires in the Caroní River basin.
  • Passive restoration of savanna, forest and moriche palm swamp ecosystems.
  • Reduction of emissions from biomass burning.
  • Prevention of forest fires, including risk estimation, prevention and reduction processes.
  • Development of processes linked to knowledge management and the exchange of information and experiences in integrated fire management
  • Fuel management in forests.
  • Prescribed burns in indigenous communities.

In the Caroní River basin, a very evident forest fire dynamic persists in savanna ecosystems, affecting the forests and moriche palm swamps located near them, causing losses of cover, soil, biological diversity and water resource quality, habitat fragmentation and loss, soil erosion and contamination, savannization and ultimately landscape modification. This phenomenon is accentuated in the current landscapes of the Gran Sabana, where the presence of human population has historically been reported through the Pemón indigenous communities, who in their traditional world hold a dominant view of fire, considering it an element that brings joy to the Pemón, to their home and their land; thus fire is present in numerous aspects of Pemón life and is also part of the Pemón's self-definition as “savanna people”.

Measure No. 2

Training for fire management in Amazonas state. GCP/VEN/11199/GFF

Strengthen indigenous community capacities in integrated fire management in the Amazon basin.

It is limited to Amazonas state.

Communities reach agreements on fire management.

In Amazonas state, the practice of fire management is ancestral in nature and a symbol of spirituality; however, due to the effects of climate change in the intervention area, the occurrence of vegetation fires may increase.

Measure No. 1

Integrated fire management program. MINEC- GCP /VEN/023/GFF

If the measure is not implemented in the Caroní River basin, the savanna ecosystem will continue to be the most affected by the occurrence of vegetation fires, which in many cases are not fought and directly affect forest edges.

In the case of Amazonas state, vegetation fires could continue to affect 1.6% of the surface area of Amazonas state.

By not developing a system for the prevention and reduction of forest fires in the Caroní River basin incorporating indigenous communities, government institutions and others, the consequence will be failure to reduce damage in the landscape units of sectors 5 and 6 of the Caroní River Basin

Communities will not take adequate measures to prevent the traditional use of fire from causing fires and the loss of forests, affecting biodiversity and ecosystem services.

Communities do not join fire management activities and the incidence of fires is minimized.

Coordination among state institutions, indigenous communities and other stakeholders to integrate efforts and human and material resources for the protection of landscape units will be hindered.

It will achieve:

  • The strengthening of technical and operational capacities for integrated fire management in the Caroní River basin (Bolívar State) and in Amazonas state.
  • Communities join fire management activities and the incidence of fires is minimized.
  • Fire prevention and management make it possible to maintain and replicate restoration strategies.
  • The reduction of the frequency of vegetation fires.
  • The reduction of emissions from biomass burning due to accidental or prescribed events.
  • The passive restoration of savanna, forest and moriche palm swamp ecosystems, through the control of forest fires as one of the stressors that prevents the natural recovery of these ecosystems.
  • Geospatial monitoring and evaluation for sustainable and integrated landscape management with emphasis on the study of fires (before, during and after), in the forest, moriche palm swamp and savanna ecosystems of the Caroní River basin, and estimation of GHG applying IPCC methodology.
  • The reduction of forest fires and the effective management of biological corridors and forest ecosystems to increase their resilience to climate variability and change

M22. RESTORATION OF ECOSYSTEMS AND LANDSCAPES

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

The implementation of ecosystem and landscape restoration will increase the capacity of ecosystems to sequester carbon and mitigate the effects of climate change, and will strengthen the resilience of ecosystems and communities to the impacts of climate change.

General description

Measures No. 1 and 2 to be implemented involve a combination of active and passive restoration strategies and techniques aimed at improving livelihoods and food security and low-emission, resilient sustainable production, considering governance and planning frameworks with indigenous communities with a gender, generational, worldview and intercultural approach.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

Regional.

Measures No. 1 and 2. Located in Amazonas state and Bolívar state (Caroní River Basin).

Gases (GHG)

Capture of CO2 eq

Avoided GHG emissions

Line of action or initiatives
  • Identification and inventory of degraded ecosystems, analysis of causes and definition of the applicable restoration mechanism.
  • Application of restoration, conservation and management mechanisms and strategies for degraded forests and landscapes.
  • Integrate the needs and knowledge of communities.
  • Conservation of forest heritage as a carbon sink and protection of species and habitats in their natural environment to preserve biological diversity.
  • Promotion of low-emission and resilient livelihoods, sustainable production and food security, governance and planning with indigenous communities with a gender, generational, worldview and intercultural approach.
  • Co-management: for forest management, to guarantee their long-term conservation and allow the sustainable use of TFP and NTFP.
  • Apply active restoration strategies and techniques in degraded areas that contribute to food security.
  • Amazonas state is a highly biodiverse territory, with a great variety of ecosystems that provide multiple ecosystem services; it is important for water resources and plays a role in climate regulation and the capture of greenhouse gases. • The Caroní River basin constitutes an area of national and global importance, mostly protected under the designation of Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE), with high biological diversity, strategic production of water and clean hydroelectric energy (it provides about 70% of the country's hydroelectric energy), mineral wealth and the presence of ancestral indigenous peoples with their traditions and ways of life.

Type of instrument

Territorial and operational

The Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela attaches high importance to development compatible with environmental protection, as expressed in the objectives of the Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019-2025, which establishes in its Objective 5.1. Protect and defend the permanent sovereignty of the State over its natural heritage and wealth, for the supreme benefit of our People, who will be its main guarantor, as well as a contribution to life on the planet. Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25

  • Fifth Historical Objective. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

6.1. Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism.

These NDC measures and actions are also framed within the National Strategy for the Conservation of Biological Diversity 2024-2030. Kunming-Montreal action targets for 2030: Target 2: Ensure that by 2030 at least 30% of areas of degraded terrestrial ecosystems are under effective restoration, in order to enhance biological diversity and ecosystem functions and services, ecological integrity and connectivity. Target 10: Ensure that areas under agriculture, aquaculture, fisheries and forestry are managed sustainably. Target 11: Restore, maintain and enhance nature's contributions to people, including ecosystem functions and services, such as regulation of air, water and climate, soil health, pollination and reduction of disease risk, as well as protection from natural hazards and disasters, through nature-based solutions and ecosystem-based approaches for the benefit of all people and nature. This NDC also contributes to the country's voluntary targets for the National Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) Strategy by 2030, which include increasing forest cover by 262.361 ha, reducing the incidence of forest fires by 50% and the natural regeneration of shrubland and grassland cover as forests

Measure No. 1

Restoration of degraded areas in the Caroní River basin with a gender, generational and intercultural approach.

MINEC- GCP/VEN/023/GFF

Restore degraded areas in the Caroní River basin with a gender, generational and intercultural approach.

It will make it possible to restore forest ecosystems to increase biodiversity and will increase carbon capture, to mention some of the improvements in ecosystem services.

Actions in the Caroní River basin

The Network of Indigenous Productive Open Classrooms (RAAPI) will be formed, made up of the Agricultural Technical Schools (ETAs) located in the sectors near the areas to be restored (sectors 5 and 6). Training through the learning-by-doing method of at least 3.000 students from these ETAs is envisaged.

1.170 ha of restored forests will mitigate -179.106 tCO2eq

Restoration actions will be established in tropical humid forest ecosystems.

The forest restoration approach covers Sustainable Forest Management (SFM) practices (agroforestry systems, reforestation) with the participation of indigenous and criollo communities and in alliance with the institutions present in the area. These approaches will seek to promote the recovery of degraded habitats to generate connectivity between natural forest fragments for the conservation of biological diversity; restore areas to improve and enhance the functioning of areas containing high conservation values; help generate sources of food and sustainable livelihoods for communities; promote restoration in watercourse protection areas to improve water regulation, favor soil stabilization to prevent erosion and foster the formation of topsoil. The conservation of biological diversity and carbon sequestration are cross-cutting issues that will be taken into account in the design and implementation of the restoration approaches.

The development of agroforestry systems (AFS) will be oriented toward the recognition of traditional and ancestral knowledge, the integrated use of native species, the valorization of non-timber forest products and the improvement of the conuco, so as to diversify and prolong production and promote the agri-food security of the families and communities settled in the Caroní River basin and Amazonas state. Efforts will be made to combine the traditional agricultural crops of indigenous communities with native and multiple-use tree and palm species to promote diversified production and the sustained use of both conucos and fallows, and productive backyards.

Reforestation will seek to establish species whose main function is to protect soils and reduce the risks of landslides and floods, as well as contribute to the regulation of the hydrological cycle, using labor from the beneficiary communities as a participatory work system through seed collection, nursery production, the plantations themselves and their cultural care. The forest plantations to be implemented in the identified area will promote the participation of indigenous and local communities in the area, the conservation of biodiversity and the multiple use of the forest. With this reforestation approach, areas that were deforested due to land-use changes will be restored, through the establishment of mixed plantations involving a diversity of native species that are accepted by the communities involved.

It will support initiatives aimed at improving livelihoods and the adoption of sustainable production practices with indigenous and criollo communities that generate new complementary income for participants' households, applying best practices to reduce the impact of productive activities on the landscape and biological diversity

The measure seeks to ensure that, in the implementation area, unsustainable management activities in conservation areas and other priority areas of the landscape are replaced by sustainable natural resource management practices.

Measure No. 2

Participatory community action plans for restoration and co-management in ABRAE and other territories.

MINEC-GCP/VEN/11199/GFF

Apply nature-based mitigation measures through landscape restoration, which allows restored ecosystems to act as carbon sinks by capturing CO2 from the atmosphere and storing it in their biomass and soil.

This measure in restored ecosystems will also make it possible to increase the resilience of landscapes and communities to extreme events

Implement actions in Amazonas state:

i) ecosystem restoration through reforestation to improve livelihoods: planting trees to restore degraded forests, increase forest cover and improve carbon capture, (ii) co-management: managing forests to guarantee their long-term conservation while allowing the sustainable use of TFP and NTFP, (iii) natural carbon sinks: protecting and restoring forests that act as carbon sinks, (iv) sustainable agriculture: agricultural practices that conserve biodiversity, improve soil fertility and reduce dependence on agrochemicals, (v) aquaculture: to promote food security and guarantee the long-term viability of fish populations and their ecosystems, and (vi) protection of species and habitats in their natural environment to preserve biological diversity

These actions will make it possible to achieve:

  • 11 participatory community action plans for restoration and co-management in ABRAE.
  • Total 1550 ha restored:
  • 700 ha through multiple-use forest or fruit tree plantations for conservation in ABRAE.
  • 300 ha of secondary vegetation recovered through natural succession processes in ABRAE.
  • 500 ha restored through agroforestry systems in ABRAE.
  • 50 ha of landscapes under improved practices with communities in areas outside ABRAE.
  • 292.436 tC02-e of GHG mitigated as a result of carbon sequestration from 1.550 ha of restored areas.

Improve the use and exploitation of forest-derived products and services by indigenous communities, considering gender equality, rural youth and environmental sustainability.

The measure seeks to ensure that ecosystems and productive lands provide goods and services to meet current and future needs while contributing to the sustainable development of land use by indigenous communities. Technical support from extension workers will be provided to strengthen community capacities for sustainable land management and forest co-management; it will make it possible to implement socioeconomic initiatives incorporating agroforestry practices for the extraction of medicinal food products of high nutritional value, as well as the use of timber and non-timber forest products (TFP and NTFP) to diversify the local economy, complementing fishing and manufactured products.

Landscape restoration faces significant challenges:

  • Scale and ambition.
  • Complexity of ecosystems.
  • Knowledge gaps.
  • Adopting adaptive approaches.

If the measures are not implemented, this may have negative impacts on biodiversity, the regional climate and the local communities that depend on the forest for their subsistence.

The implementation of the measures will make possible:

i) Addressing the protected terrestrial areas created or under improved management for conservation and sustainable use, ¡i) the area of land restored. Both will have a powerful modulating effect on the impacts associated with climate variability, iii) support for indigenous communities in the diversification of livelihoods for sustainability in landscape management and carrying out productive socio-management. Likewise, the information systems to be strengthened will directly address the monitoring and evaluation of climate variables that help in territorial decision-making.

Both measures, once implemented, will contribute to the conservation of forests and biological diversity, helping to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promoting the resilience of forest ecosystems to the impacts of climate change; in addition, they will contribute to the diversification of livelihoods, improving the food and economic security of indigenous communities, respecting their rights and ancestral knowledge, and guaranteeing their well-being and sustainability in an environment.

M23. CAPACITY-BUILDING OF THE FORESTRY SECTOR WITHIN THE TRANSPARENCY FRAMEWORK OF THE PARIS AGREEMENT

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Strengthen institutional and community capacities to improve the quality, timeliness, accessibility and usability of forest-related data, in line with the requirements of the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) of the Paris Agreement, the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory (INGEI), the forest resources assessment (FRA) and the tracking of progress made in the implementation and fulfillment of the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC)

General description

Formulation and implementation of a project for capacity-building of the forestry sector at the national level within the Transparency framework of the Paris Agreement, and continuation of the local-level promotion of participatory forest monitoring initiated with GEF Project ID 5410. “Sustainable forest management and forest conservation from an eco-social perspective” (Bolívar State) in other areas of the country, with the establishment of multipurpose plots in Amazonas state and the Caroni river basin.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National. Capacity-building project within the transparency framework of the Paris Agreement.

Regional.

  • Participatory forest monitoring in the Caroní river basin and Amazonas state with the establishment of 36 permanent multipurpose plots (24 permanent multipurpose plots in the Caroní river basin (Bolívar State) and 12 permanent multipurpose plots in Amazonas state).

Gases (GHG)

CO2 net

Line of action or initiatives

Continue capacity-building, knowledge exchange and awareness-raising in the Forestry sector within the Transparency framework of the Paris Agreement

Continue promoting participatory forest monitoring with a gender, generational, worldview and intercultural approach under development in the processes of collecting, analysing and disseminating forest-related data.

Provide the information needed to track progress made in the implementation and achievement of the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC)

Type of instrument

Territorial and Operational.

Link to Venezuelan State policies

The Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela attaches high importance to development compatible with environmental protection, as expressed in the objectives of the Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019-2025, which sets out in its Objective 5.1. Build and promote the ecosocialist historical social model, based on respect for the rights of Mother Earth and the living well of our people..., aimed at the rational, optimal and sustainable use of natural resources, respecting the processes and cycles of nature. 5.2. Protect and defend the permanent sovereignty of the State over its natural heritage and wealth for the supreme benefit of our People, who will be its main guarantor, as well as a contribution to life on the planet.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan for the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907,24/05/25

  • Fifth Historical Objective. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.
  • Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.
  • Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of cosocialism.

These NDC measures and actions are also framed within the National Strategy for the Conservation of Biological Diversity 2024-2030.

Measure No. 1

Formulation and implementation of the project for capacity-building of the forestry sector.

Build institutional and community capacities of the forestry sector within the Transparency framework of the Paris Agreement.

Participatory and inclusive national project Venezuelan State institutions, communities and companies of the Venezuelan forestry sector.

Apply improvements in the quality, timeliness, accessibility and usability of forest-related data, in line with the requirements of the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) of the Paris Agreement, the Forest Resources Assessment reports (FRA), the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory (INGEI) and the tracking of progress made in the implementation and achievement of the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC).

Makes it possible to have information on forest ecosystems and their associated biological diversity, integrated into a national information system, as a basis for their monitoring and land-use planning.

Data will be obtained on carbon pools, living and dead biomass, and soil organic carbon. With this information, statistical models will be adjusted and geospatial analysis will be improved using a geographic information system (GIS). The objective is to obtain continuous surfaces of above-ground biomass (AGB), below-ground biomass (BGB) and soil organic carbon (SOC). The resulting estimates will help identify areas with greater carbon capture and critical carbon areas; this information will be incorporated into the zoning and regulation of the management and use regulation plans (PORU) in areas under special administration regime (ABRAE).

Subject to international financing.

People from institutions and from Indigenous and criollo communities become interested, motivated and participate in the training, are empowered and apply knowledge of participatory forest monitoring, for sustainable and integrated landscape management and the conservation of biological diversity.

Train Indigenous and criollo communities in the construction and installation of community rain gauges and in the establishment and measurement of permanent multipurpose plots to collect data on greenhouse gas (GHG) flows and stocks and on forest cover and biomass in general.

  • Establish 12 permanent multipurpose plots in the Caroní river basin and Amazonas state.

Establishment of 12 permanent plots, selected based on the representativeness of forest types, following the multipurpose sampling protocol established in GEF project ID 5410.

Train Indigenous communities in the establishment and measurement of permanent multipurpose plots to collect data on greenhouse gas (GHG) flows and stocks and on forest cover and biomass in general. In addition to other biological diversity variables.

M24. NATIONAL REFORESTATION PLAN

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Mitigate the effects of climate change, protect biodiversity and guarantee the availability of natural resources for future generations. Raise environmental awareness among the population and promote a culture of respect and care for nature.

General description

The National Reforestation Plan seeks to continue the forestry sector policy in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, taking the leading participation of local communities as the strategic axis for conserving the forest heritage.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National coverage.

Gases (GHG)

CO2 capture Avoided GHG emissions

Line of action or initiatives

Recovery of river basin areas, prioritizing the country's most important reservoirs that supply water for human consumption and irrigation, to guarantee the availability and sustainable management of water. Involve the Ecosocialist Councils of the Communal Circuits, students, militia members, and workers in general in reforestation processes with forest and fruit species in the recovery of rural and urban spaces with high ecological potential.

Type of instrument

Territorial and operational

Homeland Plan 2019-2025

5th historical objective: Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

5.1. Build and promote the ecosocialist historical social model, based on respect for the rights of Mother Earth and the living well of our people, developing the principle of

Link to Venezuelan State policies

unity within diversity, the integral and systemic vision, popular participation, the role of the nation-State, the incorporation of technologies and forms of organization of production, distribution and consumption, aimed at the rational, optimal and sustainable use of natural resources, respecting the processes and cycles of nature.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907,24/05/25

Sixth transformation “Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism. • Massive reforestation process of river basins and actions against soil desertification and the consequent loss of agricultural soils. • Green corridors and humanizing public space. National policy for urban reorganization and beautification. • 11: Strengthen training and awareness campaigns and community participation in preservation and conservation tasks, tree planting, recovery of water sources and green spaces.

Legal framework: The Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela stipulates in its article 127 the obligation of the State to guarantee that the population lives in an environment free of pollution, where the air, water, soils, coasts, climate, ozone layer and living species are specially protected. In this same context, the Forest Law, in its article 8, delegates to the Executive Power the exercise of stewardship over national forest policy, which must be applied in order to guarantee the sustainability of forests and the other constituent elements of this heritage.

M25. INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT OF MULTIPLE-USE AND HIGH CONSERVATION VALUE LANDSCAPES FOR THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF THE VENEZUELAN ANDEAN REGION

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Reduce and reverse degradation in productive landscapes of the Venezuelan Andean region to create an enabling environment for the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity, with emphasis on simultaneous agroforestry systems (SAF) and Forestry systems (SF) that contribute to the livelihoods of local populations and global environmental benefits.

General description

Institutional and community capacities for territorial management with landscape, environmental sustainability, gender-sensitive and multiple-use approaches strengthened; area (ha) under improved management in the buffer zones of the Areas Under Special Administration Regime (ABRAE) increased; gender-sensitive sustainable management practices in productive landscapes, contributing to increased productivity, the establishment of sustainable product supply chains and the conservation of biological diversity through Agroforestry Systems (SAF); market strategies support the conservation and sustainable use of forest ecosystems and sustainable production in the selected municipalities of the Andean region; monitoring and evaluation strategy developed for reporting the progress and results achieved by the project in implementing its work plans under the principle of adaptive management, through objectively verifiable indicators and means of verification; private sector venture with farmers from Mérida for the establishment of climate-smart agroforestry systems.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

The actions are implemented in the external buffer zones of ABRAE (six National Parks and two natural monuments) in 14 municipalities of the Venezuelan Andean region, namely: Bolívar municipality of Barinas state; Andrés Eloy Blanco and Morán municipalities of Lara state; Andrés Bello, Campo Elias, Caracciolo Parra y Olmedo, Miranda, Rangel and Tulio Febres Cordero Municipalities of Mérida state; Monseñor luán Vicente de Unda, Ospino and Sucre municipalities of Portuguesa state; and Boconó and luán Vicente Campo Elías municipalities of Trujillo state. For the private sector venture, the scope is limited to Mérida state.

Gases (GHG

The restoration of degraded forest and agricultural lands will mitigate some 2.392.849 metric tons CO2 eq

Line of action or initiatives
  • Institutional and community capacities for territorial management. • Increase in the area (ha) under improved management in the buffer zones of the ABRAE. • Restoration of degraded forest lands. • Restoration of degraded agricultural lands. • Implementation of sustainable management practices in coffee and cocoa agroforestry systems.* Establishment of climate-smart agroforestry and silvopastoral systems.

Type of instrument

Territorial and operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

The Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela attaches high importance to development compatible with environmental protection, as expressed in the objectives of the Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019-2025, which establishes in its Objective 5.1. Build and promote the ecosocialist historical social model, based on respect for the rights of Mother Earth and the living well of our people, aimed at the rational, optimal and sustainable use of natural resources, respecting the processes and cycles of nature. 5.2. Protect and defend the permanent sovereignty of the State over its natural heritage and wealth, for the supreme benefit of our People, who will be its main guarantor, as well as a contribution to life on the planet.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907,24/05/25.

Fifth Historical Objective: Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism. These NDC measures and actions are also framed within the National Strategy for the Conservation of Biological Diversity 2024 - 2031.

Kunming-Montreal action targets for 2030: Target 2: Ensure that by 2030 at least 30% of areas of degraded terrestrial ecosystems are under effective restoration, in order to enhance biological diversity and ecosystem functions and services, ecological integrity and connectivity. Target 10: Ensure that areas under agriculture, aquaculture, fisheries and forestry are managed sustainably. Target 11: Restore, maintain and enhance nature's contributions to people, including ecosystem functions and services, such as regulation of air, water and climate, soil health, pollination and reduction of disease risk, as well as protection from natural hazards and disasters, through nature-based solutions and ecosystem-based approaches for the benefit of all people and nature. This NDC also contributes to the country's voluntary targets for the National Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) Strategy to 2030, which include increasing forest cover by 262.361 ha, reducing the incidence of forest fires by 50% and the natural regeneration of shrubland and grassland cover as forests. These actions are also linked to the Misión Árbol Ecosocialista, the Gran Misión Agro Venezuela, the National Planting Plan Programme 2019-2025 and the National Reforestation Plan 2022-2025.

Measure No. 1

Institutional and community capacities for territorial management.

Strengthen institutional and community capacities for the management of territorial use, and sustainable production and management in multiple-use landscapes and high conservation value forests.

15 actors with capacities for the management of 237.000 ha of land in 14 selected municipalities in the Venezuelan Andes.

The sustainable management of productive systems ensures a constant and diversified production of food and natural resources. By achieving better yields, pressure from the expansion of the agricultural frontier into natural forests is also reduced

Stakeholder involvement and degree of community ownership.

Measure No. 2

Improved land management in the ABRAE buffer zones of the project area.

Improve current land use in the ABRAE buffer zones through the conservation and rehabilitation of ecosystems, as well as the implementation of good agricultural and livestock practices, in order to conserve, restore, use and improve ecosystem and economic structure, functionality and productivity.

The implementation area is 300.000 ha distributed across the ABRAE buffer zones of 14 selected municipalities in the Venezuelan Andes.

Through the implementation of the Management Plans and environmental education, the biodiversity of the ecosystems and agroecosystems present in the ZAM is conserved, ecosystem functions are safeguarded, and the availability of water, the proper functioning of watersheds, risk reduction, the conservation of wetlands, the mitigation of global warming and adaptation to its effects, and pollution reduction, among others, are ensured.

Stakeholder involvement and degree of community ownership.

Measure No. 3

Restoration of degraded forest lands

Restore degraded forest lands, in peripheral protection zones of national parks and protective zones of water bodies, through both passive and active restoration techniques, including reforestation, prevention and control of vegetation fires, environmental awareness-raising and the establishment of fences.

The implementation area is 1.246 ha distributed across the ABRAE buffer zones of 14 selected municipalities in the Venezuelan Andes.

The restoration of degraded lands has a wide range of associated benefits, including: climate change mitigation, the recovery of ecosystem services, soil protection and increased biodiversity, among others.

Capacity-building and financing are required.

Measure No. 4

Restoration of degraded agricultural lands

Restore degraded agricultural lands through the establishment of coffee and cocoa agroforestry systems and various alternative diversified cropping systems.

The implementation area is 4.000 ha distributed across the ABRAE buffer zones of 14 selected municipalities in the Venezuelan Andes

Address the cultural barriers that limit the implementation of agroforestry systems and their sustainability.

Measure No. 5

Implementation of sustainable management practices in coffee and cocoa agroforestry systems.

Increase productivity and the establishment of agroforestry product chains.

237.000 ha of agricultural land with agroforestry systems, sustainable and community forest management, agroecological production and good practices.

Higher yields and better incomes, which reduces pressure from the expansion of the agricultural frontier into natural forests.

Strengthen capacities and achieve coordination among key actors in the agroforestry product supply chain.

Measure No. 6

Promotion and establishment of climate-smart agroforestry and silvopastoral systems with coffee farmers and producers in Mérida state
  • Climate change mitigation: The trees in the SACCS capture carbon from the atmosphere, which helps to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change.
  • SACCS can increase the productivity and diversity of agricultural systems, which improves the food security of communities.
  • SACCS foster biological diversity by creating habitats for various species of plants, animals and insects.
  • SACCS provide a range of ecosystem services, such as water regulation, pollination and pest control.

It is an action that also contributes to Adaptation to climate change, since SACCS help farmers adapt to the impacts of climate change, such as droughts, floods and extreme temperatures. The diversity of species and the improvement of soil health make the systems more resilient to these events.

Stakeholder involvement, and availability of own and external resources for farmers in Mérida to carry out the actions linked to the SACCS.

M26. NATIONAL LAND DEGRADATION NEUTRALITY (LDN) STRATEGY

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Promote actions aimed at preventing, mitigating or offsetting the effects of desertification and drought, as a mechanism to achieve Land Degradation Neutrality (NDT).

General description

The National Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) Strategy consists of reversing desertization and desertification processes, as well as mitigating the effects of droughts by assessing global data on Land Cover, carbon stocks and land productivity. Framed within 5 major strategic objectives.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National. It will focus on the recovery of 7.910,5 km2 (791.050,00 ha) of degraded land representing 1,08% of the national territory, as part of the National Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) Strategy.

Regional. It will focus on intervention in 11 priority basins from a physical-natural and socioeconomic standpoint for the conservation and sustainable use of forests and biodiversity, generating adequate soil management with agriculture and agroforestry, achieving the conservation of water resources, among others.

Gases (GHG)

Conservation of carbon sinks and avoided GHG emissions

Line of action or initiatives

Strengthening of the normative and regulatory framework for soil conservation and management processes. • Institutional and community capacities for the management of Land

Degradation Neutrality (LDN). • Land areas with improved land cover. • Land areas with improved productivity. • Land areas with increased organic carbon.

Type of instrument

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Territorial, regulatory and operational for the adequate implementation of Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN).

The Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela attaches high importance to development compatible with environmental protection, as expressed in the objectives of the Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019-2025, which sets out in its “Objective 5.1. Build and promote the ecosocialist historical social model, based on respect for the rights of Mother Earth and the living well of our people...”, aimed at the rational, optimal and sustainable use of natural resources, respecting the processes and cycles of nature, as well as what is indicated in objective 5.2. Protect and defend the permanent sovereignty of the State over its natural heritage and wealth for the supreme benefit of our People, who will be its main guarantor, as well as a contribution to life on the planet. Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25

Promotion of actions aimed at preventing, mitigating or offsetting the effects of land degradation

Measure No. 1

Promotion of actions aimed at preventing, mitigating or offsetting the effects of land degradation

In 2019, Venezuela reported an area of 129.394,30 km2 of degraded areas, representing 14,41% of the country's total area.

In this regard, if the seven measures are not implemented, the main causes of soil degradation in 17 states of the country may increase; the most relevant direct factors of land degradation are indicated to be: a) Inadequate management of annual, perennial, shrub and tree crops; b) Deforestation and removal of natural vegetation; c) Overexploitation of vegetation for domestic use; d) Overgrazing; and e) Urbanization and infrastructure development.

The condition of affected ecosystems will be improved, and desertification and land degradation will be combated, to contribute to land degradation neutrality in the national territory.

M27. SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Implement forest management practices for the conservation of forests and the sustainable development of the forestry engine, promoting an increase in forest cover.

General description

Access to the forest and forest heritage takes place through sustainable forest management, defined by the Forest Law (2013) as “the set of practices based on scientific or traditional knowledge, associated with the forest heritage. It encompasses continuous development in a given area from the allocation of forest land use to the generation of its products, with the objective of maintaining the structure and functions of forest ecosystems and generating environmental, social and economic benefits”; it is implemented through forest management plans in both natural and planted forests aimed at maximizing collective well-being and guaranteeing environmental, social and economic sustainability. The specific actions considered under this measure for the purposes of this NDC include: • Forest restocking and/or reforestation in intervened areas as environmental compensation, recovery and improvement of the forest. • Promote the increase of forest cover at the national level through the management of planted forests (forest plantations). • Application of silvicultural techniques for the conservation and improvement of natural forest. • Demarcate Wild Environment Reserve Areas on rural properties, to conserve ecological balance and protect the forest heritage, biological diversity and genetic resources. • The development of these actions promotes the conservation and management of forests as carbon sinks.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

Avoided emissions and capture of Carbon dioxide CO2

Line of action or initiatives

Application of prior environmental control instruments for sustainable forest management. Application of current legal regulations on forestry and environmental matters. Application of the ecosystem approach to sustainable forest planning and management. Promote the establishment of managed planted forests to increase and diversify forest productive potential, as well as carbon sinks. Traceability of forest products.

Type of instrument

Territorial and operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

The Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela attaches high importance to development compatible with environmental protection, as expressed in the objectives of the Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019-2025, which sets out in its Objective 5.1. Build and promote the ecosocialist historical social model, based on respect for the rights of Mother Earth and the living well of our people..., aimed at the rational, optimal and sustainable use of natural resources, respecting the processes and cycles of nature. 5.2. Protect and defend the permanent sovereignty of the State over its natural heritage and wealth for the supreme benefit of our People, who will be its main guarantor, as well as a contribution to life on the planet.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan for the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907,24/05/25.

Fifth Historical Objective. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

6.1 Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism.

These NDC measures and actions are also framed within the National Strategy for the Conservation of Biological Diversity 2024- 2030.
