M28. RELAUNCH OF THE MISIÓN ÁRBOL FOUNDATION

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Revitalize Misión Árbol to vigorously undertake the recovery, conservation and sustainable use of forests, ecological balance and the recovery of degraded areas, through the protagonistic participation of People's Power, organized communities and environmental movements.

Encourage collective ecological awareness of the importance of forests, ecological balance and the recovery of degraded spaces, particularly among those living in rural areas, promoting a new environmentalist ethic to improve the quality of life of the Venezuelan population, the rescue and protection of flora, as well as to settle the historical debt that the population has with our ecosystem.

General description

The Misión Árbol Foundation is the entity responsible for seed collection, plant production, planting, maintenance, recovery, conservation and sustainable use of forests, for the improvement of the population's quality of life, the rescue and protection of flora, as well as to settle the historical debt that the population has with our ecosystem, promoting the recognition of Environmental Rights and the Rights of Mother Earth in the Ethics of the New Woman and Man.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National coverage

Gases (GHG)

CO2 capture and avoided GHG emissions

Line of action or initiatives
  • Construction of community and school nurseries for the production of fruit and forest plants.
  • Carrying out plantations for protective and agroforestry purposes to conserve the environment, contribute to a new productive model and improve the community's quality of life.
  • Development of a sense of belonging in communities to guarantee the maintenance and protection of plantations.
  • Promotion of citizen participation in the planning and execution of reforestation projects.
  • Environmental education to raise awareness of the importance of forests and environmental conservation.

Type of instrument

Territorial and operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019-2025

5th historical objective: Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

5.1. Build and promote the ecosocialist historical social model, based on respect for the rights of Mother Earth and the living well of our people, developing the principle of unity within diversity, the comprehensive and systemic vision, popular participation, the role of the nation-state, the incorporation of technologies and forms of organization of production, distribution and consumption, aimed at the rational, optimal and sustainable use of natural resources, respecting the processes and cycles of nature.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031:

Sixth Transformation, Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

No. l: Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism.

No. 4: Massive process of reforestation of watersheds and actions against soil desertification and the consequent loss of agricultural soils.

No. 10: Green corridors and humanizing public space. National policy for urban reorganization and beautification.

No. ll: Strengthen training and awareness campaigns and community participation in preservation and conservation tasks, tree planting, recovery of water sources and green spaces.

Legal framework: The Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela stipulates in its article 127 the obligation of the State to guarantee that the population develops in an environment free of pollution, where the air, water, soils, coasts, climate, ozone layer and living species are specially protected. Misión Árbol is based on article 127 of the Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, which establishes the right and duty of each generation to protect and maintain the environment, and on the provisions of the Forest Law (2013).

M29. ESTIMATION OF CARBON CAPTURED IN FORESTS ESTABLISHED AND SAFEGUARDED BY PDVSA

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Estimate the amount of carbon fixed in the biomass of 14.423 Hectares (Ha) consisting of the Compensatory Forests established by PDVSA, Subsidiaries and Joint Ventures (3.289 Ha), protection forests (9.713 Ha) and production forests (1.421 Ha) located in the areas of influence of oil and gas industry operations, as well as in the protective zones under PDVSA's custody.

General description

Develop a methodology for estimating the amount of carbon fixed in the biomass of the Compensatory and production Forests established by PDVSA, Subsidiaries and Joint Ventures, in addition to conservation forests (ABRAE), which are under the protection and custody of the oil and gas industry; these, in turn, function as carbon sinks and are distributed across different watersheds nationwide. This action contributes to the National Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Mitigation Plan.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

Carbon dioxide (CO2)

Line of action or initiatives

Develop and apply over a period of five (5) years a methodology to estimate the amount of carbon fixed in the biomass of 14.423 hectares consisting of the Compensatory and production Forests established by PDVSA, Subsidiaries and Joint Ventures, located in the areas of influence of the oil and gas company's operations, as well as in the protective zones (ABRAE) under PDVSA's custody. It is important to note that these forests, in their growth phase, consume atmospheric CO2 and fix it as carbon in their biomass, helping to reduce the country's GHG emissions and providing oxygen to the planet.

Type of instrument

Territorial and Operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies
  • Homeland Plan 2019-2025, Objective 5.4.2: Design a mitigation plan covering the GHG-emitting productive sectors, as a national voluntary contribution to the efforts to save the planet. In line with the provisions of the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations (2025-2031), specifically the (6) Sixth Transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.
  • Development of strategies to mitigate environmental impact and protection of the Amazon and natural reserves.

Link to the SDGs

SDG 9: Industry, innovation and infrastructure. SDG 13: Climate action.

SDG 15: Life on land.

Link to the INGEI

INGEI sector

4. Land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF).

IPCC codes: 3.B.I. Forest land, 3.B.2. Cropland, 3.B.3. Grassland 3.B.4. Wetlands, 3.B.5. Settlements and 3.B.6. Other land

General sectoral target according to the INGEI baseline

GHG target. Carbon fixed in the biomass of 14.423 Hectares (Ha) consisting of the Compensatory Forests established by PDVSA, Subsidiaries and Joint Ventures

Implementing entity or entities

Ministry of People's Power for Hydrocarbons, through the Vice Ministry of Oil, Vice Ministry of Gas, Vice Ministry of Hydrocarbon Geopolitics, Vice Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Productive Efficiency in Hydrocarbons, Vice Ministry of Petrochemicals and Refining and PDVSA.

Development and application of a methodology to estimate the amount of carbon fixed in the biomass of the Compensatory, production and conservation Forests established and under the custody of PDVSA, Subsidiaries and Joint Ventures.

Measure and manage environmental impact by obtaining precise data on the amount of carbon that forests are absorbing, fixing and transforming, which is crucial for assessing their contribution to Climate Change mitigation.

Corporate Sustainability through the quantification of carbon capture in forest biomass

States: Miranda,

Anzoátegui, Monagas, Barinas, Portuguesa, Apure, Cojedes, Trujillo, Táchira, Zulia and Falcón.
  • Use the methodology to measure and improve the carbon footprint, aligning sustainability strategies with Climate Change mitigation objectives.
  • The methodology contributes to the conservation of natural resources by promoting sustainable forestry practices.
  • Forests act as carbon sinks, absorbing CO2 from the atmosphere and storing it in their plant tissues.
  • Carbon fixation helps offset GHG emissions from other industrial and human activities.
  • Proper management of Compensatory Forests fosters biodiversity, supporting a wide range of both fauna and flora species.
  • Limitations to carrying out detailed measurement of tree dasometric variables in some areas.

  • Heterogeneity in the composition (high biodiversity) and structure of forests can lead to variations in carbon capture, which adds complexity to a real estimation of net carbon balances in the Compensatory and conservation Forests under PDVSA's protection.

M30. ESTABLISHMENT OF FORESTRY AND AGROFORESTRY SYSTEMS AS CARBON SINKS FOR THE ENVIRONMENTAL RECOVERY OF NATURAL AREAS

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Continue establishing forestry and agroforestry systems for the environmental and ecological recovery of degraded areas within the river basins prioritized by the Governing Body, as a compensatory measure for the environmental impacts generated by oil activity, as well as establishing new natural areas as carbon sinks in contribution to the National Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Mitigation Plan.

General description

Implement and establish agroforestry systems on 1.838 Hectares (Ha) in the areas of influence of oil and gas industry operations, which will enable the environmental and ecological recovery of degraded areas under the protection and custody of PDVSA, in 12 States of the national territory, for the period (2025-2030).

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

Carbon dioxide (CO2)

Line of action or initiatives
  • Develop forest restocking activities aimed at the monitoring and control of the Compensatory Forest projects to be established by the various PDVSA organizations, with emphasis on the hectares requested and also those recognized by the Ministry of People's Power for Ecosocialism (MINEC), as well as the hectares to be planted and the hectares of forests under maintenance that serve as carbon sinks, which contribute to the National GHG Mitigation Plan.
  • Continue the establishment of forestry and agroforestry systems for the environmental and ecological recovery of degraded areas within the watersheds prioritized by the Governing Body, as a compensatory measure for the environmental impacts generated by oil activity, as well as the establishment of new natural areas as carbon sinks contributing to the National GHG Mitigation Plan.
  • Apply active restoration strategies and techniques in degraded areas under the protection and custody of PDVSA.

M31. STRENGTHENING OF TECHNOLOGICAL AND REGULATORY CAPACITIES IN INTEGRATED WASTE MANAGEMENT

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Enable the collection, systematization and tracking of activity data for the phases or stages of integrated waste management at the national level, required for estimating GHG emissions at final disposal sites, through the application of the IPCC methodology, and comply with the INGEI principles and the tracking of NDC progress. This action is directly linked to the sectoral INGEI improvement plans.

General description
  • The design and launch of an Observatory is envisaged as a “technical tool for the use of optical images for the monitoring, follow-up, reporting and evaluation of integrated waste management”. • Acquisition and installation of equipment enabling the monitoring, follow-up and evaluation of waste management nationwide. • Construction of the system of management and environmental performance indicators to track progress in Emission reductions in integrated waste management nationwide and the annual INGEI report.» Implementation of the National Registry for Waste Management with daily, monthly and annual reporting frequency.» Strengthening of the regulatory framework for integrated waste management.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National, Regional and municipal

With pilot implementation at prioritized final disposal sites.

Gases (GHG)

CH4, CO2

Line of action or initiatives
  • Strengthening of integrated waste management. • Strengthening of technological capacities for the operational management of final disposal sites. • Generation of activity data with greater accuracy, completeness, consistency and coherence for the estimation of GHG emissions at final disposal sites. • Promote research to determine specific emission factors at municipal final disposal sites. • GHG estimation applying IPCC methodologies. • Proposal to reform the Law on Integrated Waste Management. • Establish standards for the environmentally safe and sustainable integrated management of non-hazardous solid residues and waste that contribute directly and indirectly to GHG reduction.

Type of instrument

Territorial, Operational and Regulatory.

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 - 2025.

Historic Objective No. 5. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

5.5.1.7. Generate, strengthen and sustain a national policy with urban applications of the solid waste system, assuming its integral conception, in the generation, collection, deposition and use of solid waste, taking into account the economic, training, cultural and technological variables, as well as the environmental variables of the system.

5.5.1.7.6. Generate public policies on dumps and sanitary landfills, as well as their environmental, health and ecological variables.

5.5.1.7.7. Develop policies for risk mitigation and reduction of environmental impact in the solid waste collection and final disposal system.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031:

Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism.

Legal Framework

Law on Integrated Waste Management (Official Gazette No. 39.584, dated 30 December 2010), the Law on Hazardous Substances, Materials and Waste (Official Gazette No. 5.554, dated 13 November 2001), Decree No. 2216 “Standards for the Management of Solid Waste of Domestic, Commercial, Industrial or any other Non-Hazardous origin” (Extraordinary Official Gazette No. 4.418, dated 27 April 1992), Decree No. 230 “Sanitary Standards for the Design and Operation of a Sanitary Landfill for Non-Toxic Solid Waste” (Extraordinary Official Gazette No. 34.600, dated 22 November 1990), and Decree No. 2635 “Standards for the Control of the Recovery of Hazardous Materials and the Management of Hazardous Waste” (Extraordinary Official Gazette No. 5.245, dated 03 August 1998).

M32. PILOT PLAN FOR THE OPERATIONAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL RECOVERY OF FINAL DISPOSAL SITES

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Implement the pilot plan for the operational and technological recovery of prioritized final disposal sites in order to reduce Carbon Dioxide equivalent emissions by 3,33% (183.751 Gg CO2 eq) by 2030.

General description
  • Conducting studies for planning the operational management of prioritized final disposal sites. • Acquisition and commissioning of machinery for the orderly disposal of scattered residues and waste and controlled operation of prioritized final disposal sites. • Strengthening of capacities for the operational management of prioritized final disposal sites. • Implementation of the operational management of prioritized final disposal sites. • Construction of the gas and leachate collection and treatment system. • Monitoring of GHG gases with annual frequency (Flow and composition CH4, CO2). • Monitoring of leachates with annual frequency (Flow, Composition Parameters BOD, COD, heavy metals).

Scope and coverage of the NDC

Regional States of Zulia, Monagas, Portuguesa and Guárico

Gases (GHG)

CH4, CO2

Line of action or initiatives
  • Strengthening of integrated waste management. • Strengthening of capacities for the operational management of final disposal sites. • Reduction of GHG emissions at prioritized final disposal sites. • Adequate operational management of final disposal sites to convert them into managed sites, according to the IPCC classification. • Environmental remediation of areas surrounding the final disposal site. • Reduction of problems associated with groundwater pollution. • Reduction of problems associated with air pollution. • Reduction of problems associated with disease vectors.

Type of instrument

Territorial and Operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 - 2025 Historical Objective No. 5. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species. 5.5.1.7. Generate, strengthen and sustain a national policy with urban applications of the solid waste system, assuming its integral conception, in the generation, collection, deposition and use of solid waste, taking into account the economic, training, cultural and technological variables, as well as the environmental variables of the system. 5.5.1.7.6. Generate public policies on dumps and sanitary landfills, as well as their environmental, health and ecological variables. 5.5.1.7.7. Develop policies for risk mitigation and reduction of environmental impact in the solid waste collection and final disposal system. M33. NATIONAL PROGRAM FOR THE MONITORING AND CONTROL OF GHG EMISSIONS IN THE THERMAL TREATMENT PROCESS.

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Design and implement by 2030 the national program for the monitoring and control of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions generated by companies authorized by the Ministry of People's Power for Ecosocialism through the Registry of Activities Capable of Degrading the Environment (RACDA), operating in the activity of thermal treatment (incineration) of hazardous materials and waste, in order to establish a baseline, assess its evolution, and establish options for improvement in meeting the GHG reduction and reporting target.

General description

» Diagnostic survey and technical follow-up of companies authorized in the Registry of Activities Capable of Degrading the Environment that carry out thermal treatment activities in incinerators, for the quantification of GHG emissions generated in thermal treatment (incineration) processes. » Acquisition of portable measurement equipment for the quantification of GHG emissions generated by companies authorized through the Ministry of People's Power for Ecosocialism that carry out thermal treatment (incineration) of hazardous waste and materials. » Strengthening of capacities in the handling of greenhouse gas monitoring and control equipment.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

Territorial, Operational and Regulatory

Gases (GHG)
  • Carbon dioxide (CO2) • Carbon monoxide (CO)
  • Nitrous oxide (N2O) • Sulfur dioxide (SO2)
  • Nitrogen oxide (NOX) • Methane (CH4)
  • Ammonia (NH3)

Line of action or initiatives

The process of incinerating hazardous waste has a significant climate impact that contributes significantly to the greenhouse effect, while also producing dioxins, furans and polychlorinated biphenyls, substances that are hazardous to the atmosphere. Faced with this reality, the Venezuelan State has generated regulatory instruments to reduce and control emissions to the atmosphere produced by the operation of polluting sources, such as incinerators, so as to ensure air quality and the well-being of the population and other living beings, in accordance with the parameters established in national standards and in compliance with the international agreements signed by the country.

Type of instrument

Operational and Regulatory

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 - 2025.

Great historical objective V. Contribute to the preservation of life on the Planet and the salvation of the human species.

5.4. Contribute to the formation of a great global movement to contain the causes and repair the effects of climate change occurring as a consequence of the predatory capitalist model.

5.1.4.1.1. Strengthen and develop the regulatory framework on industrial policies and practices, as well as the generation of waste and polluting particles in the air or water.

5.2.1.2.2. Promote clean industrial technologies that guarantee effluents and emissions with less need for treatment for their purity.

ORGANIC LAW OF THE HOMELAND PLAN OF THE 7 GREAT TRANSFORMATIONS 2025-2031, G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25.

Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

Objectives 7. State policy for waste, as well as materials and components of the industrial process and their compatibility with environmental protection.

Objective 13. Awareness campaigns for the proper management of waste in the community. Improve, standardize and inform the community of the schedules for waste disposal and collection. Improve equipment in communities for garbage disposal.

Legal Framework

  • Water and Air Quality Law Official Gazette No. 6.207, 28 December 2015
  • Decree No. 638 - Standards on air quality and control of atmospheric pollution Official Gazette No. 4.899 dated 19 May 1995.

M34. ENTERPRISE FOR THE SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF ORGANIC WASTE

I. Policies, measures and actions:

Objective

It is an innovative and sustainable initiative that seeks to transform organic waste into a valuable resource for agriculture and gardening. This project is based on the principle of the circular economy, where waste becomes raw material for new products, thereby reducing the amount of waste sent to final disposal sites, which contributes to reducing methane and nitrous oxide emissions.

General description

The process of producing substrate from organic matter from urban and agro-industrial waste consists of several stages:

  • Waste collection and sorting
  • Composting: The sorted organic matter undergoes a composting process, which is the controlled decomposition of organic matter by microorganisms in the presence of oxygen. Composting is carried out in piles or special containers, where temperature, humidity and aeration are controlled to optimize the decomposition process.
  • Maturation and stabilization of the compost.
  • Mixing and conditioning of the mature compost.
  • Packaging and distribution of the substrate

Scope and coverage of the NDC

Municipal coverage | Gases (GHG)

CEU, C02,N20

Line of action or initiatives
  • Reduction of the amount of organic waste at final disposal sites.
  • Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions
  • Processing of organic matter from urban solid and agro-industrial waste for the production of substrates.

Type of instrument

Territorial and operational

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan of the Nation 2019-2025

Historic Objective No. 5. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

5.5.1.7. Generate, strengthen and sustain a national policy with urban applications of the solid waste system, assuming its integral conception, in the generation, collection, disposal and use of solid waste, taking into account the economic, training, cultural and technological variables, as well as the environmental variables of the system.

Measure No. 1

Production of substrate from the processing of organic matter from urban and agro-industrial waste.
  • There is no contribution to decreasing the amount of organic waste sent to final disposal sites, which leads to the emission of greenhouse gases.
  • There is no contribution to the reduction of the use of chemical fertilizers

In general terms, when the measure is implemented at the municipal level:

  • The amount of organic waste sent to dumps decreases, which reduces pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
  • Organic waste is transformed into a valuable resource, generating a useful product for agriculture and gardening.
  • It contributes to improving soil quality, since substrate made from compost improves soil structure, fertility and water retention capacity, which favors plant growth.

* It contributes to reducing the use of chemical fertilizers, since organic substrate provides nutrients to plants naturally, which reduces . the need to use chemical fertilizers, which can be harmful to the environment and human health.

  • It promotes more sustainable and environmentally friendly agricultural practices, by using a renewable resource and reducing dependence on chemical inputs.
  • It can generate employment in the collection, processing and distribution of organic waste, as well as in the production and marketing of the substrate.

I. Policies, measures and actions:

Objective

Implement a school-level composting system in the Girardot and Santiago Mariño municipalities of Aragua state to manage organic waste.

General description

Composting is a key strategy to reduce these emissions and promote the circular economy. This project is based on the principle of the circular economy, where waste becomes raw material for new products, thus reducing the amount of organic waste and residues sent to final disposal sites, which contributes to the reduction of methane emissions.

  • There is no contribution to decreasing the amount of organic waste sent to final disposal sites, which leads to the emission of greenhouse gases.

In general terms, when the measure is implemented at the municipal level:

  • It contributes to improving soil quality, since substrate made from compost improves soil structure, fertility and water retention capacity, which favors plant growth.
  • It contributes to reducing the use of chemical fertilizers, since organic substrate provides nutrients to plants naturally, which reduces the need to use chemical fertilizers, which can be harmful to the environment and human health.

M36. STRENGTHENING OF THE NATIONAL RECYCLING PROGRAM FOR THE RECOVERY OF NON-HAZARDOUS WASTE

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Strengthen the recovery of non-hazardous waste (plastic, cardboard, paper, glass, organics, among others) through recycling, in order to reduce waste at final disposal sites. This will help contribute to the mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions.

General description

Seven measures are established with their respective actions for the recovery of non-hazardous waste that contribute to reducing its volumes at final disposal sites. Likewise, monitoring and follow-up of the National Plan will be carried out through indicators that make it possible to measure progress and support decision-making.

Scope and coverage of the NDC

Local, Regional and National

GHG Gases)

Carbon Monoxide (CO) Sulfur Dioxide (SO2) Particulates. Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs)

Line of action or initiatives

The Venezuelan State has the obligation, with the active participation of society, to guarantee that the population develops in an environment free of pollution, where the air, water (...) are specially protected, in accordance with the law, and likewise to reduce and control emissions to the atmosphere produced by the operation of polluting sources, so as to ensure air quality and the well-being of the population and other living beings, in accordance with the parameters established in the regulating standards and in compliance with the international agreements signed and ratified by the country.

From this perspective, and to meet this commitment, the country, through the Ministry of People's Power for Ecosocialism, proposes a set of initiatives whose actions are aimed at Strengthening recycling, through: - Raising awareness among the Venezuelan population about the sorting of non-hazardous recoverable materials at source through environmental education. - Strengthening the circular economy through various programs and projects, such as the Technical Recycling and Cleaning Committees (METRAS) and the National Registry of Handlers of Non-Hazardous Recoverable Materials (RENMA), enabling the productive linkage of public and private companies for the process of transforming non-hazardous recoverable materials. - The organization of communities through the formation of technical recycling and cleaning committees (METRAS), where processes of social oversight and knowledge about the behavior of waste in the territories are generated. - Strengthening of actions to increase the recycling rate in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

Type of instrument

Territorial, Operational and Regulatory

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Third Socialist Plan for the Economic and Social Development of the Nation 2019 - 2025.

Great historical objective V. Contribute to the preservation of life on the Planet and the salvation of the human species.

5.4. Contribute to the formation of a great global movement to contain the causes and repair the effects of climate change occurring as a consequence of the predatory capitalist model.

5.1. 4.3.4. Promote waste sorting by the population, institutions and public, communal and private companies, through the development of training and awareness campaigns, development of logistics capacities, and collection centers.

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations (2025-2031):

Sixth transformation: Ecosocialism, Science and Technology.

Strengthen State policy for the preservation of life on the planet, the fight against climate change and the construction of ecosocialism.

Focus of action: Modernization and Environmental monitoring system. Achieve an automated monitoring system for effluents and emissions, connecting emitting industries with control institutions.

Legal Framework

  • Law on Integrated Waste Management Official Gazette No. 39.584, dated 30 December 2010.
  • Law on Hazardous Substances, Materials and Waste, Official Gazette No. 5.554, dated 13 November 2001.

M37. INSTITUTIONAL STRENGTHENING FOR THE REGULATION AND MANAGEMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY IN THE WASTEWATER TREATMENT AND DISCHARGE SECTOR

I. Policies, measures and actions

Objective

Carry out a national diagnosis during the period 2025-2030 in order to verify the operability of public and private treatment plants for discharges and liquid effluents (domestic and industrial), so as to create methodologies to inventory the generation of the greenhouse gases methane and nitrous oxide, in order to implement policies, measures and actions to promote the progressive reduction of these gases and contribute to the fight against the climate crisis.

General description
  • Update of the Law on Water and Air Quality and of Decree No. 883 “Standards for the Classification and Control of the Quality of Water Bodies and Liquid Discharges or Effluents”.
  • Preparation of a national diagnosis to verify the operability of public and private treatment plants for liquid discharges and effluents (domestic and industrial).
  • Carry out the inventory, estimation and/or quantification of the baseline related to greenhouse gas emissions (methane and nitrous oxide) in wastewater and industrial treatment plants.
  • Acquisition of twelve (12) pieces of equipment (online methane and nitrous oxide analyzers), to verify the generation of these gases in the treatment plants for liquid discharges and effluents of public and private companies.
  • Determination of infrastructure conditions and needs for the safe management of environmental quality specifically in the wastewater treatment and discharge sector

Scope and coverage of the NDC

National

Gases (GHG)

Methane (CH4) and Nitrous Oxide (N2O)

Line of action or initiatives

Modernization and environmental monitoring system

The Venezuelan State has the obligation, with the active participation of society, to guarantee that the population lives in a pollution-free environment, where air, water (...) are especially protected, in accordance with the law, and likewise to reduce and control emissions into the atmosphere produced by the operation of polluting sources, so as to ensure the quality of water and liquid discharges and effluents, as well as the well-being of the population and other living beings, in accordance with the parameters established in the standards that regulate it and in compliance with the international agreements signed and ratified by the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

Type of instrument

Territorial, Operational and Regulatory

Link to Venezuelan State policies

Articles 127,128 and 129 of the Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

Third Socialist Plan of the Nation 2019-2025

Historical Objective No.5 Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

5.5.1.7. Generate, strengthen and sustain a national policy with urban applications of the solid waste system, assuming its integral conception, in the generation, collection, deposition and use of solid waste, taking into account the economic, training, cultural and technological variables, as well as the environmental variables of the system.

5.5.1.7.7. Develop policies for risk mitigation and reduction of environmental impact in the solid waste collection and final disposal system. In this case it applies to the wastewater treatment and discharge sector

Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations (2025-2031):

Fifth Historical Objective. Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species.

Chapter IV. Adaptation NDC

Adaptation to climate change has become a global challenge. As the world faces extreme weather events that threaten life on the planet, adaptation emerges as an essential response to protect communities and ecosystems; for this reason, it is recognized in the Paris Agreement, which establishes that not only must greenhouse gas emissions be reduced, but also the resilience of countries must be strengthened, especially those most vulnerable to the effects of climate change.

The Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) on adaptation ratifies the commitment to adaptation in the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031 (G.O. No. 6907, 24/05/25).

This Plan sets out the strategic lines of impetus for: i) the civilizational offensive against the climate crisis and ii) strengthening and expanding the national adaptation plan, as a State policy, to prepare the country for climate scenarios and impacts, accelerated by the civilizational crisis of capitalism.

Despite the challenges imposed by the Unilateral Coercive Measures (MCU), which have limited access to financial and technological resources, Venezuela reaffirms its determination to move forward in tackling the climate crisis with the creation of the Gran Misión Madre Tierra Venezuela, which will also make it possible to continue progressing in meeting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the 2030 Agenda and the global goal on adaptation established in the Paris Agreement (Figure 4.1).

Figure 4.1. The Nation's Economic and Social Development Plans, the Gran Misión Madre Tierra and their alignment with global commitments for adaptation to climate change.

This effort reflects the country's decision to contribute to the salvation of the human species, where adaptation is not only a response to impacts, but also an opportunity to promote the satisfaction of needs with equity and with deep respect for nature.

The process of building this Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) on adaptation (Figure 4.2) considers: i) the analysis of climate scenarios and the vulnerabilities of sectors to them and ii) the inclusion of the most vulnerable actors and groups, under the principles of participation of People's Power and the public and private sectors, within the enhanced transparency framework, in accordance with decisions 4/CMA.1, 5/CMA.3, 9/CMA.1 and 18/CMA.1.

Figure 4.2. Work route for strengthening the NDC on adaptation

This ensures that the proposed adaptation targets (2025- 2030) achieve the satisfaction of the needs of the Venezuelan people to increase resilience to the climate crisis, based on the financial resources required to increase adaptive capacity in the period 2025-2030.

National adaptation objective

The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela recognizes the high value of the participation of all social actors involved, the multiple levels of government and public-private linkages or arrangements, for increasing the resilience of the Bolivarian people to climate change; in this sense, the national adaptation objective established for the Second NDC considers:

Increasing adaptive capacity, through the establishment of sectoral targets that make it possible to reduce vulnerability to climate change and increase resilience, through: i) the mainstreaming of adaptation in the planning process of high-impact policies, programs, projects and actions and ii) the promotion of the empowerment of People's Power and the public, private and academic sectors in the fight against the climate crisis.

This within the framework of an enabling environment, in which international cooperation and climate finance make it possible to drive concrete actions for adaptation to the effects of climate change, considering common but differentiated responsibilities.

Impacts of climate change

According to the recent National Climate Change Vulnerability Assessment Report of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, climate scenarios indicate that precipitation will decrease in most of the national territory, with significant alterations in its seasonality and possible changes in the onset of the rainy season, which has implications for rainfed agriculture and water resources management due to an accentuation of drought.

Likewise, climate scenarios show a clear trend toward a generalized increase in mean monthly temperature, which would notably alter the country's thermal pattern. The greatest climatic variation would occur in the city of San Cristóbal, followed by Mérida and Ciudad Guayana. In Caracas, Maracay and Valencia, notable reductions in precipitation would be observed (especially under the most critical climate scenario).

Moderate reductions in precipitation in the city of Porlamar also stand out. However, as for Mérida, the changes have repercussions not only for city inhabitants, but also for tourism activities and, consequently, for the local economy.

In urban areas, decreased water availability can lead to drinking water shortages, affecting health and economic activities. Extreme climate events such as floods can force the displacement of people, putting pressure on other settlements and increasing the vulnerability of the affected population.

In addition, the impacts of climate change can gradually affect livelihoods and increase poverty and inequality in urban areas. On the other hand, rising temperatures and water scarcity can spread diseases and affect public health.

For the agriculture sector, simulations indicate that rainfed crops such as maize, sorghum, soybeans and beans could experience a significant decrease in their yields due to climate change.

In the area of agricultural lands of maximum preservation, high vulnerability affects lands in the states of Monagas, Miranda, Aragua, Carabobo, Cojedes, Portuguesa, Lara, Barinas, Táchira, Mérida, Trujillo. Meanwhile, medium vulnerability extends over lands in Anzoátegui, Guárico, Zulia and Falcón, where both vulnerability categories occur.

Both decreases in precipitation rates and rising temperatures would affect the country's agri-food security. The effects derived from these impacts translate into increased water stress, impacts on crop development, growth and yield, greater incidence of pests and diseases, increased demand for irrigation water and reductions in irrigated areas.

Of the hydrographic regions, the most affected by decreases in precipitation are Central, Lago de Valencia and Llanos Centrales, and the greatest temperature increases would be recorded in Amazonas, Bajo Apure and Caroní; the latter region would be the most vulnerable to climate change and is considered the one with the greatest surface water storage in the country.

The effects derived from this decrease in flows and aquifer recharge will translate into potential water stress, which will worsen as water consumption increases, whether due to the growth of human populations or to increased requirements of the resource for agricultural, industrial and hydroelectric uses.

On the other hand, variations in climate drivers would increase the occurrence of extreme rainfall that could cause losses and damages. For example, 65,32% of the stations of the hydrometeorological monitoring and climate prediction system in the country are located in zones of medium sensitivity; therefore, extreme variations in the drivers can trigger effects with potential damage from droughts or from intense rainfall, floods or mass movements in the areas where these hydrometeorological stations are located. This situation can affect the network infrastructure and, consequently, cause discontinuity in the monitoring of climate variables.

In the social sphere, decreases in precipitation rates, high temperatures and the occurrence of extreme weather events can affect the livelihoods and quality of life of the population, which may promote human displacement due to severe climatic conditions.

At least 54 municipalities in the country are considered to have high and very high vulnerability values with a potential risk condition that could cause human displacement.

This could translate into future economic losses from damage to infrastructure, disruption of productive activities, high reconstruction costs and impacts on human life.

Analysis of climate projections indicates that both sea level and sea surface temperature (SST) will experience variable rates of increase. These changes can have significant direct impacts and multiple problems affecting people, due to the increase in extreme events, floods, growing coastal erosion and the consequent loss of land surface. In the latter case, the states of Anzoátegui, Falcón, Nueva Esparta and Sucre revealed the most critical values in the sea-level rise projections.

Similarly, a reduction in annual precipitation is expected in all indigenous communities, the most affected being those located in the Gran Sabana, with decreases of up to 530 mm, followed by those located in Perijá, with 301 mm, those settled in the east of Amazonas state, with 284 mm, those of the Orinoco Delta, with 240 mm, and those in the Gran Goajira, with 231 mm.

Temperature increases would reach 2,5 °C for the communities of the Gran Sabana. In the case of eastern Amazonas state, an increase of 2,20 °C is predicted, and for those located in Perijá, the Gran Goajira and the Orinoco Delta, 2,18 °C; 1,8 °C and 1,79, respectively. The impacts derived from this climate variability would affect the way of life of indigenous peoples, owing to their close relationship with nature, their dependence on natural resources for subsistence and their traditional knowledge systems, factors that make them particularly susceptible to negative impacts on the environment; therefore, climate change represents a significant threat to these communities.

In the country, the employed economically active population (EAP) is also considered vulnerable to climate change; communal, social and personal services represent the most affected labor force in terms of the number of workers. In general terms, in the most critical scenario, 60% of the country's population shows medium vulnerability to climate change, in those areas with lower population, while in 26% of the territory, specifically in Sucre, part of Zulia, the country's llanos states and the Lara-Falcón system, high vulnerability is projected.

Given the progression of climate change, it is also estimated that Natural Areas will be affected, which in turn will impact biological diversity. The natural areas most affected in the most critical scenario, by category, will be Waraira Repano National Park (NP) and Macarao NP; in the Natural Monuments (NM) category, Cerro Santa Ana and Pico Codazzi; in the Wildlife Refuge (RFS) category, Ciénaga de Los Olivitos followed by Laguna Boca de Caño; in the Wildlife Reserve (RSF) category, Ciénaga de la Palmita e Isla de Pájaros and Tucurere RSF; and in the Biosphere Reserve (RB) category, the Alto Orinoco-Casiquiare RB.

Finally, the basic and university education sectors, as well as youth, are considered agents in the fight against climate change, whose purpose is to reduce vulnerability and increase the resilience of the population to climate change.

Proposal of national Adaptation strategies and measures by sector

Through this document, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela presents the enabling and implementing measures to reduce the intensity of impacts and the vulnerability associated with the climate crisis, in order to increase the resilience of the nation's physical-natural and social systems, in compliance with the decisions established in the UNFCCC, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Paris Agreement (2015). To compile the information, a standardized sheet was prepared for building the measures, comprising three stages and 14 elements (Figure 4.3).

Figure 4.3. Elements considered in the formulation of the NDC on adaptation

As a result of this methodological approach to building the Adaptation NDC, the Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) meets criteria of value, relevance, feasibility and scope, in order to materialize the nation's fifth historical objective “Contribute to the preservation of life on the planet and the salvation of the human species” and the sixth transformation, Ecosocialism, Science and Technology, contemplated in the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan for the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031, and the lines of action established in vertices 3 “Territory for life” and 4 “Climate for life” of the Gran Misión Madre Tierra Venezuela.

In this context, the descriptive sheets of the NDC on adaptation for the period 2025-2030 will be presented at the end of this chapter, after the National Adaptation Plan sheet. The contributing sectors are listed in Table 4.1.

National Plan for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources sectors

From the perspective of “shared but differentiated responsibilities”, the Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has established as State policy a series of actions related to adaptation to climate change and to the commitments assumed within the framework of the UNFCCC.

The country is committed to strengthening responsibility in the face of climate change, a commitment that materializes in State policies and management instruments from the highest levels, such as the Homeland Plan 2019-2025. This Plan sets the strategic objectives associated with climate policy in Historical Objective No. 5.4.3, which expresses the need to “Design a National Adaptation Plan that enables the country to be prepared for climate scenarios and impacts.

Likewise, the Organic Law of the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031 sets out, in its 6T - Ecosocialism, Science and Technology, the strategic line “National Adaptation Plan in the face of the climate crisis generated by capitalism”, together with what is established in the Gran Misión Madre Tierra Venezuela in vertices 3 “Territory for life” and 4 “Climate for life”.

The design of the proposal takes into consideration the Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA) approach, which includes the use of biological diversity and environmental services in a comprehensive adaptation strategy that seeks food security, guaranteeing the population's access to water in adequate quantity and quality, availability of water resources to ensure productive and sustainable development, conserving and protecting water bodies from pollution and reducing extreme events associated with lack or excess of water. Likewise, this readiness support program generates cultural, social and economic benefits, among which the positive collateral impacts on public health, local development, hydroelectric generation and watershed conservation stand out. The design of the NAP is developed through an inclusive and participatory process that addresses the priorities and actions of the nation, linked to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with a focus on EbA solutions and other complementary measures, including gender, indigenous peoples and private sector considerations. The products that will support the results are presented below, in the Descriptive Sheet of the NAP NDC, and are expected to be completed within a period of thirty-six (36) months from its start (in September 2024).

National Plan for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources sectors

A1. NATIONAL PLAN FOR ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE CHANGE IN THE AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES AND WATER RESOURCES SECTORS

Context analysis

11 Problem definition

The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela is considered a country highly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change, according to the categories established in the UNFCCC; this is evidenced in the vulnerability assessment presented in the country's Third Communication on Climate Change and Biennial Transparency Report. Considering the above, agriculture, fisheries and water resources are considered vulnerable sectors and have been prioritized by the Venezuelan State in the design of the first National Plan for Adaptation to Climate Change.

2 | Beneficiaries and users

  • Beneficiaries: The inhabitants of the Communes and Communal Circuits.
  • Users: Groups most vulnerable to climate change in the Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources sectors, such as small-scale farmers and fishery and aquaculture producers, and the private sector.

Adaptation actions

3 | Adaptation vision

Strengthening of adaptation planning capacities in the agriculture, fisheries and water resources sectors, to contribute to food and water security with a focus on Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM), and development of activities that strengthen a long-term financing framework for adaptation to climate change.

4 | Value proposition

  • The development of the NAP requires the establishment of governance mechanisms among the different national and regional social actors, all with the objective of strengthening communication and promoting participation and coordination in the design and future implementation of the NAP among the administrative levels of the decision-making bodies.
  • Improve and generate hydrological information and information on climate scenarios, vulnerability levels and climate change impacts in the agriculture, fisheries and water resources sectors, standardization of methodologies and proposals for adaptation measures.
  • Promote private sector participation in adaptation to climate change, based on the principle of co-responsibility in environmental management in the nation.

5 | Adaptation options

  • Outcome 1. Strengthening of adaptation planning governance and institutional coordination.
  • Outcome 2. Evidence base created to design and integrate adaptation solutions into sectoral planning for maximum impact.
  • Outcome 3. Promotion of private sector participation in adaptation.
  • Outcome 4. Financial strategy for the sustainability of adaptation.

6 | Key activities

Outcome 1.

  • Establishment of a governance framework for the development and implementation of the NAP.
  • Establishment of a communication strategy that includes a gender equality and non-discrimination approach and the participation of indigenous communities and the private sector.
  • Climate change adaptation training program for government decision-makers.
  • Design of a Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) System
  • Compilation of lessons learned in the design of the NAP.

Outcome 2.

  • Strengthening of the monitoring and information system and network for climate and hydrological variables
  • Vulnerability assessment for the NAP target sectors.
  • Proposal of adaptation measures and ecosystem-based adaptation solutions.

Outcome 3.

  • Context analysis and capacity building, enabling environment and coordination mechanism for private sector participation in the implementation of adaptation actions. Outcome 4.
  • Development of a long-term financing framework for adaptation to climate change.
  • Design of a National Adaptation Fund for the Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources sectors.
  • Development of a concept note for priority sectors.

7 | Type of adaptation options and measures

It is considered an institutional option and an enabling measure whose objective is to strengthen the capacity of Venezuelans to adapt to climate change in the agriculture, fisheries and water resources sectors.

Governance for adaptation

8 | Benefits and co-benefits

  • Consolidation of coordination between administrative levels of decision-making bodies and vulnerable groups in the agriculture, fisheries and water resources sectors.
  • Design of a plan that enables the agriculture, fisheries and water resources sectors to adapt to climate change.
  • Strengthening of the country's climate services.
  • Promotion of the importance of private sector participation in adaptation actions.
  • Establishment of a financial strategy that makes the sustainability of the Plan viable.

9 | Key metrics

Indicators:

  • Number of participatory territorial workshops with People's Power.
  • Number of attendees at the participatory territorial workshops with People's Power.
  • Number of participants in the climate change adaptation capacity-building program.
  • Number of roadmaps for strengthening the monitoring and information system and network for climate and hydrological variables.
  • Number of climate change vulnerability assessments in the prioritized sectors.
  • Number of proposals for climate change adaptation measures and EbA solutions.
  • Number of documents with guidelines for the integration of the private sector in climate change adaptation.
  • Number of documents with a financial strategy for climate change adaptation.
  • Number of documents with the design of a national adaptation fund for the agriculture, fisheries and water resources sectors.

Targets (2025-2030):

  • 39 participatory territorial workshops with People's Power.
  • 3120 attendees at the participatory territorial workshops with People's Power.
  • 480 participants in the climate change adaptation capacity-building program.
  • 1 roadmap for strengthening the monitoring and information system and network for climate and hydrological variables.
  • 3 climate change vulnerability assessments in the prioritized sectors.
  • 03 proposals for climate change adaptation measures and EbA solutions.
  • 01 document with guidelines for the integration of the private sector in climate change adaptation.
  • 01 document with a financial strategy for climate change adaptation.
  • 01 document with the design of a national adaptation fund for the agriculture, fisheries and water resources sectors.
  • 01 (validated) document with the National Plan for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources sectors.

  • INAMEH.
  • MinMujer.
  • MPPPI.
  • MPPP.
  • Vulnerable population.
  • Private Sector.
  • Universities and Research Centers.

Older Adults Sector

A2. ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT PROGRAM IN THE CARE CENTERS OF THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF SOCIAL SERVICES (INASS)

Sector: Older Adults

Context analysis

11 Problem definition

Older people are particularly sensitive to the effects of climate change; exposure to extreme heat and other intense weather events entails impacts on physical and mental health, which would also have a cumulative effect on people with disabilities and/or chronic medical conditions, those who live alone, have inadequate nutrition or live in spaces unsuitable for withstanding the high temperatures associated with climate change. Hence the need to adapt practices to face the climate crisis in the care centers of the National Institute of Social Services (INASS) at the national level.

2 | Beneficiaries and users

Beneficiaries: Older persons and/or older adults (rural, indigenous and urban communities) of the INASS Care Centers.

Users: Older persons and/or older adults and INASS.

Adaptation actions

3 | Adaptation vision

Promote management for adaptation to climate change in the Care Centers of the National Institute of Social Services (INASS) at the national level, through the integration of actions and social transformations necessary to minimize the intensity of the effects of climate change on the community of older adults served, and thereby increase the sector's resilience to the onslaught of the climate crisis.

4 | Value proposition

  • Reduce vulnerability levels in the older population, considering criteria for improving environmental performance for the protection of older adults in the face of climate variability, in the Care Centers of the National Institute of Social Services (INASS) at the national level.
  • Increase the quality of life of older adults in the Care Centers of the National Institute of Social Services (INASS) at the national level

5 | Adaptation options

  • Rational use of water resources.
  • Water sowing.
  • Awareness-raising regarding the impacts of climate change and its effects.
  • Vulnerability assessment studies.

6 | Key activities

  • Create spaces in each center for a water harvesting system.
  • Carry out workshops on socio-environmental risks related to climate change.
  • Carry out workshops and create campaigns on environmental education.
  • Carry out reforestation activities. Create nurseries of ornamental, fruit and medicinal plants.

7 | Type of adaptation options and measures

The environmental management program in the Care Centers of the National Institute of Social Services (INASS) is considered both an institutional option (programs) and an enabling measure for adaptation to climate change.

Governance for adaptation

8 | Benefits and co-benefits

The use of these measures combines economic, social and environmental benefits, improving the quality of life of older adults through the promotion of a healthier and more sustainable environment. Economic benefits include savings in drinking water payment costs; social benefits are expected to include improved safety, well-being and emergency response capacity of older adults.

9 | Key metrics

Indicators:

  • Number of INASS created in strategic areas of the country.
  • Number of activities carried out.
  • Number of persons of older-adult age benefited.
  • Volume of water harvested.

Targets (2025-2030):

  • 40% of care centers implement the environmental management program for the fight against climate change.
  • 2 awareness-raising activities per year per care center.
  • 1 water harvesting system per care center.

10 | Key actors

  • Ministry of People's Power for Older Adults, for grandfathers and grandmothers.
  • MINEC.

External financing is required

Agriculture Sector

A3. COMPREHENSIVE AGRICULTURAL HEALTH COMMITTEES (COSAI)

Sector: Agriculture

Context analysis

11 Problem definition

Agro-productive activities at the national level require consideration of specific actions for the use and promotion of sustainable agricultural practices that strengthen the adaptation of agricultural producers to climate change, in order to minimize the negative (multidimensional) impacts on Agricultural Production: decreasing yields, deteriorating product quality, emergence of resistant pests and diseases; which leads to increased production costs, as well as risks to Public Health and the Environment. To guarantee the sustainability of agricultural production and the conservation of natural resources, the organization of agricultural communities is essential, so as to motivate and facilitate support for producers in the use of climate-smart agriculture practices.

2 | Beneficiaries and users

  • Beneficiaries: Agricultural producers (small, medium and large), organized community and technicians of the National Institute of Comprehensive Agricultural Health (INSAI).
  • Users: Agricultural producers and organized community, National Institute of Comprehensive Agricultural Health (INSAI) and all those involved in the agricultural and livestock production chain.

Adaptation actions

3 | Adaptation vision

Promotion of the Comprehensive Agricultural Health Committees (COSAI) at the national level, to promote sustainable agricultural practices as a measure of adaptation to climate change.

4 | Value proposition

  • Increase the number of new COSAI in strategic areas of the country.
  • Promote the active participation of producers in COSAI activities for the promotion and use of sustainable agricultural practices for adaptation to climate change.

5 | Adaptation options

Popular Participation in Comprehensive Agricultural Health is fundamental for pursuing the purposes of the National Institute of Comprehensive Agricultural Health (INSAI). For this reason, the creation of the Comprehensive Agricultural Health Committees (COSAI) as a strategy for the popular organization of agricultural communities enables the empowerment and active participation of producers in the promotion and use of sustainable agricultural practices for adaptation to climate change.

6 | Key activities

  • Organize workshops and courses (in-person or virtual) on topics related to promoting sustainable agricultural practices as a measure of adaptation to climate change.
  • Carry out visits to production units to provide technical assistance.
  • Encourage the participation of all community members, including women and young people.
  • Facilitate the exchange of knowledge and experiences between producers and research institutions, universities and civil society organizations.
  • Promote the active participation of producers in COSAI in 75 activities for the promotion and use of sustainable agricultural practices for adaptation to climate change.

7 | Type of adaptation options and measures

The promotion of the Comprehensive Agricultural Health Committees (COSAI) is considered an institutional program option and an enabling measure for adaptation to climate change.

Governance for adaptation

8 | Benefits and co-benefits

The creation of the Comprehensive Agricultural Health Committees in the agricultural sector represents a strategic investment in terms of organization, with a high return in terms of sustainability, productivity and food security. The main benefits of this initiative include: increased productivity, improved product quality, cost reduction, access to new markets, healthier, safer and available food, conservation of biodiversity; reduced use of agrochemicals and the implementation of integrated pest and disease management practices reduce soil, water and air pollution; and sustainable agricultural practices can contribute to the adaptation of agricultural production units to climate change.

9 | Key metrics

Indicators:

  • Number of CONSAI created in strategic areas of the country.
  • Number of CONSAI formalized in strategic areas of the country.
  • Number of promotion activities.
  • Number of farmers participating in promotion activities. Targets (2025-2030):
  • Create and formalize 25 new COSAI (5 per year) in strategic areas of the country by 2030.
  • Promote the active participation of producers in COSAI in 75 (15 per year until 2030) activities for the promotion and use of sustainable agricultural practices for adaptation to climate change.

10 | Key actors

MPPAPT-INSAI, MINEC, Agricultural and livestock producers and organized community

Institutional financing.

A4. CAPACITY BUILDING FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS ON COMPREHENSIVE AGRICULTURAL HEALTH AND CLIMATE CHANGE

Sector: Agriculture

Context analysis

11 Problem definition

Capacity building is required for the technical staff of the National Institute of Comprehensive Agricultural Health and for agricultural producers in the areas of vulnerability and adaptation to climate change. Capacity building and training is a tool that would enable our agricultural producers to increase their capacity both to mitigate the causes of climate change and to adapt to its consequences.

2 | Beneficiaries and users

  • Beneficiaries: Agricultural producers (small, medium and large), organized community and technicians of the National Institute of Comprehensive Agricultural Health (INSAI).
  • Users: Producers, professionals, technicians, students, teachers, public and private institutions, and those related to the agricultural sector. All those involved in the agricultural and livestock production chain.

Adaptation actions

3 | Adaptation vision

Increase capacity building for agricultural producers on comprehensive agricultural health and climate change.

4 | Value proposition

  • Carry out capacity-building, training and support activities for agroecological or organic production for producers, at the national level, in comprehensive agricultural health.
  • Carry out training activities on vulnerability and adaptation to climate change in the field of comprehensive agricultural health.
  • Increase the participation of producers in training and awareness-raising processes on sustainable and resilient agricultural production systems.

5 | Adaptation options

Strengthening the capacities of agricultural producers is a fundamental element for the transition toward sustainable and resilient agricultural production systems. By investing in farmer training, we are investing in a more sustainable future for all.

6 | Key activities

  • Train producers in crop and soil management techniques that minimize the impacts of climate change.
  • Strengthen knowledge on the identification and management of pests and diseases, promoting the use of biological control and agroecological practices.
  • Provide training on livestock health management, disease prevention and animal welfare.

7 | Type of adaptation options and measures

Capacity building is considered a social education option and an enabling measure for adaptation to climate change.

Governance for adaptation

8 | Benefits and co-benefits

Capacity building for agricultural producers in Comprehensive Agricultural Health and climate change represents a strategy that will bear fruit in the short, medium and long term, benefiting both producers and the environment. By adopting agroecological and climate-resilient practices, producers can increase their yields and improve the quality of their products, which leads to reduced costs and fewer losses.

9 | Key metrics

Indicators: Number of training activities. Targets (2025-2030):

  • Carry out 16.200 capacity-building, training and support activities for agroecological or organic production for producers, at the national level, in comprehensive agricultural health. Between 2020 - 2024, 53,76% has been carried out, so 46,24% remains to be carried out until 2030, around 1.500 capacity-building, training and support activities for agroecological or organic production and climate change for producers annually, at the national level.
  • Carry out 18 training activities on vulnerability and adaptation to climate change in the field of comprehensive agricultural health.
  • Benefit 200.000 agricultural producers. Of the 2020 - 2024 target, 64,79% has been carried out, so 35,21% remains to be carried out until 2030, around around 14.085 beneficiaries per year, at the national level.

10 | Key actors

MPPAPT-INSAI, MINEC, Agricultural and livestock producers and organized community.

A5. SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF THE ANDEAN LANDSCAPE

Sector: Agriculture

Context analysis

11 Problem definition

In the country, agricultural and livestock activities play an essential role in the development of the country's upper basins, since they contribute to sustaining the rural economy and providing food security; however, a large percentage of these activities in the Venezuelan Andes are carried out in susceptible zones and in some cases involve: i) deforestation, ii) expansion of the agricultural frontier into non-permitted areas, iii) occurrence of forest fires, iv) degradation of ABRAE and v) replacement and abandonment of shade-grown coffee and cocoa crops. The synergy of these actions translates into loss of biological diversity and unsustainable land management.

2 | Beneficiaries and users

  • Beneficiaries: Agricultural producers (men and women), communities at the local level (direct beneficiaries) and at the regional level (indirect beneficiaries).
  • Users: Agricultural producers (men and women), ecosystems and associated biological diversity.

Adaptation actions

3 | Adaptation vision

Evidence of the reduction of forest degradation in productive landscapes of the Venezuelan Andean region, creating a favorable environment for the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity. Incorporating tree elements into production systems that ecologically benefit agricultural crops and allow product diversification.

4 | Value proposition The project will establish key actions that contribute to resolving some of the root causes, such as

  • Strengthening conservation actions at the landscape level and;
  • Boosting the development of coffee and cocoa agroforestry systems and agroecological production, as well as community agroforestry.

e 5 | Adaptation options

  • Strengthening of governance.
  • Education and awareness-raising.
  • Restoration of degraded ecosystems.
  • Development of agroforestry systems.
  • Establishment of ecological corridors.

6 | Key activities

  • Design and implementation of pilot demonstration management plans for sustainable land management.
  • Capacity development programme with an integrated landscape management (ILM) approach.
  • Development and implementation of an early warning system (EWS) in the pilot landscapes.
  • Development and implementation of the environmental education programme.
  • Training, technical assistance and agricultural extension plans with an emphasis on agroecology, AFS, SLM and SFM.
  • Monitoring and evaluation.

7 | Type of adaptation options and measures

Sustainable Management of the Andean Landscape is considered both a physical and a social option and an implementing measure for adaptation to climate change.

Governance for adaptation

8 | Benefits and co-benefits

Direct benefits: Reduction of forest degradation in productive landscapes of the Venezuelan Andean region, improvement in the yield of the productive systems of local communities. Additional benefits:

  • Environmental: recovery of biodiversity, ecosystem services and connectivity of the forests in the buffer zones of the ABRAE.
  • Economic: sustainable increase in the yield of productive systems.
  • Sociocultural: at least 30% of the beneficiaries are women.

9 | Key metrics

Indicators:

  • Sustainable land management plans designed and implemented.
  • People benefiting from the training programmes. Targets (2025-2030):
  • 14 sustainable land management plans designed and implemented for the management of 542.246 hectares.
  • 11.040 people benefiting from the training programmes.

10 | Key actors

  • MINEC, CONARE, MPPAPT, INSAI, INIA,CVC.
  • Mayors' offices and Producers (men and women).

325.000 US$

Urban Settlement Sector

A6. ACTION PLAN IN THE HOUSING SECTOR FOR ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE CHANGE

Sector: Urban Settlement Sector (Housing)

Context analysis

11 Problem definition

Climate change is affecting the natural variability of the climate, causing increasingly frequent and intense extreme events, and as a consequence this increases the loss of human lives and damage to property.

In order to bring about, on a massive and accelerated scale, the conditions for the healthy and equitable enjoyment of the social rights enshrined in the Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, the Venezuelan State creates a set of large-scale social programmes under the figure of Missions and Great Missions. This Misión Vivienda Venezuela achieves access to decent housing that meets the needs of People's Power under the principle of "housing as a social demand and not a commodity". Thus, the Mission benefits families who do not own homes and those who owned them but were affected by extreme events associated with climate change. The Mission considers innovative construction systems that incorporate local technologies, bioclimatic and environmental criteria and technology transfer (achieved through international agreements).

2 | Beneficiaries and users

Beneficiaries: General population, as well as small and large families vulnerable to climate change.

Users: MINHV, small and large families affected by extreme socio-natural events and the general population without access to housing.

Adaptation actions

3 | Adaptation vision

The Gran Misión Vivienda Venezuela, as a State policy, pursues among its objectives guaranteeing the right to decent housing in a comprehensive housing and habitat model that incorporates, among other variables, bioclimatic and environmental criteria.

4 | Value proposition

The construction of 1.840.000 homes planned from a bioclimatic and environmental perspective, under the standards of sustainable and resilient infrastructure as a basic building code, unquestionably improves all housing works that can be rehabilitated or built in suitable spaces under environmental regulations, with cost-effective measures that guarantee the well-being (buen vivir) of families within a home, and they can be complemented by improving energy efficiency, incorporating photovoltaic panels, and water efficiency, with the collection and storage of rainwater, accessibility for persons with disabilities, and green measures in housing developments that help offset the negative effects of climate change.

5 | Adaptation options

National Housing Construction and Control Plan.

6 | Key activities

  • Construction of housing throughout the national territory, aimed at providing decent conditions for Venezuelan families.
  • Training on solid waste treatment.
  • Proposal for the implementation of the Local Strategic Development Plans (PDEL).
  • Continuation of the Proposal of Indicators to Certify Projects aimed at the Construction of Sustainable Housing, framed within the fulfilment of the SDGs.

7 | Type of adaptation options and measures

The National Housing Construction and Control Plan is considered a social option and a direct measure for adaptation to climate change.

Governance for adaptation

8 | Benefits and co-benefits

  • Construction of housing to meet national demand.
  • Housing intended for the most vulnerable population, especially those who have suffered losses as a result of extreme socio-natural events.
  • Insertion of new bioclimatic and environmentally friendly construction elements, thereby reducing the carbon footprint and the water footprint.
  • Increased resilience as well as strategic planning of the housing and habitat sector.

9 | Key metrics

Indicators:

  • Number of homes built nationwide.
  • Number of homes built with alternative bio-construction systems.
  • Number of homes built with locally manufactured materials.
  • Number of new construction elements inserted in housing construction.
  • Number of Campaigns aimed at Increasing the m2 of green areas in urban spaces.
  • Percentage (%) of mitigation of pollutant elements in the housing developments built.
  • Percentage (%) of reduction of solid waste in large housing developments in Venezuela.
  • Number of animal and plant species reintegrated into their original habitat.
  • Number of Policies, Guidelines, Plans and Programmes aimed at achieving the targets set. Targets (2025-2030):
  • An estimated 5.700.000 homes are to be built in response to the housing needs of the Venezuelan people, of which 1.840.000 will be allocated in response to people affected by the effects of climate change.
  • An estimated 700.000 homes are to be built with alternative bio-construction systems (wood, bamboo, bahareque), in response to loss and damage from the adverse effects of climate change, and with special attention to rural areas, Indigenous peoples and other ecologically fragile areas.
  • The construction of an estimated 1.140.000 homes using locally produced materials, in order to reduce by 20% the emission of pollutant gases into the atmosphere resulting from transport.
  • The organization of an estimated 108 tree-planting campaigns aimed at increasing the green areas of housing developments nationwide to minimize the effects of climate change.
  • 2 sectoral plans and 9 annual plans will be developed in the habitat and housing sector, aimed at establishing the sustainability policies needed to mitigate risks from hydrometeorological hazards and steer toward the construction of housing that guarantees climate resilience.
  • 4 specific plans will be developed in the habitat and housing sector, namely: the Local Strategic Development Plan (PDEL), as a fundamental tool to guarantee the right to the city and harmony with the habitat, allowing orderly intervention in human settlements from the local level; the Comprehensive Maintenance Plan for residential buildings, aimed at mitigating 30% of pollutant elements of existing constructions; the Pilot Solid Waste Management Plan, aimed at reducing by 40% the solid waste that enters the habitat; and the Urban Forests Plan, to promote the reintegration of plant and animal species into the territorial area that was intervened.
  • An estimated 6 current housing construction standards are to be improved for the integration of natural climate variability.

10 | Key actors

MPPPHV, Gran Misión Vivienda Venezuela, MINEC and People's Power.
