Tourism Sector

A40. SUSTAINABLE TOURISM MASTER PLANS

Sector: Tourism

Context analysis

1 Problem definition

The planetary crisis lays the foundations for all sectors of society to become aware of the effects their actions have on the environment. In the case of the tourism sector, the relationship between environment and activity is bidirectional, making it clear that the sector impacts the environment, but the environment also impacts the sector. Hence, the climate crisis significantly affects the tourism activities of the regions and therefore the livelihoods of their population. In order to minimize negative repercussions, it is necessary to create planning instruments that allow the organization and better distribution of tourism space, including the analysis not only of tourism management instruments but also of climate management instruments.

2 | Beneficiaries and users

Beneficiaries: Tour operators, local communities, government entities in charge of tourism. Researchers, planners, decision-makers at the national, regional and local levels.

Users: General population, MINEC, MINTUR.

Adaptation actions

3 | Adaptation vision

Design Master Plans for Sustainable Tourism Development that guarantee the social, economic and environmental well-being of populations and their livelihoods, while reducing their vulnerability to the effects of climate change.

4 | Value proposition

Strengthen tourism destinations on the basis of projects with sustainable tourism alternatives that promote resource conservation and the well-being of communities.

5 | Adaptation options

  • Preparation of master plans incorporating climate change adaptation strategies and actions into their design.
  • Review of the legal instruments and policies supporting tourism to consider in them the adaptation of biological diversity management guidelines due to the effects of climate change.

6 | Key activities

  • Inter-institutional liaison and coordination to carry out field activities that make it possible to gather relevant baseline information.
  • Carry out the diagnoses for the preparation of the master plans.
  • Identify the climate impacts affecting the tourism sector.
  • Training to consolidate knowledge on climate change
  • Constantly carry out vulnerability assessments of tourism destinations through the implementation of a GIS that allows monitoring and analysis of information that promotes the sound proposal of climate change adaptation options and measures.
  • Include relevant climate change considerations in the design of the master plans.
  • Design sustainable tourism master plans.

7 | Type of adaptation options and measures

The design of sustainable tourism master plans is considered an institutional option and an enabling measure aimed at reducing the sector's vulnerability to climate change.

Governance for adaptation

8 | Benefits and co-benefits

  • Strengthen partnerships between the public sector, the private sector and organized communities to generate local management and land-use planning instruments, considering climate change adaptation in tourism planning strategies and tools.
  • Planning of areas with tourism potential that promote the conservation of biological diversity and the maintenance of ecosystem services.

9 | Key metrics

Indicators:

  • Number of master plans developed.
  • Number of legal instruments adapted. Targets (2025-2030):
  • 2 master plans developed.
  • 2 legal instruments adapted.

10 | Key actors

MINTUR, MINEC, Tour operators and the general population.

11 Budget and costs 550.000 US$.

12 | Sources of financing (current or future)

  • Institutional financing.
  • External financing

A41. SUSTAINABLE TOURISM MASTER PLANS (DATABASE)

Sector: Tourism

Context analysis

1 Problem definition

It is necessary to strengthen technological capacities for the geospatial representation of the tourism sector in Venezuela that allows the assessment of vulnerability to climate change impacts, its monitoring and the development of specific adaptation strategies to increase the recovery capacity of the tourism sector in the face of extreme events related to climate change.

2 | Beneficiaries and users

Beneficiaries: - Tour operators, local communities, government entities in charge of tourism. - Researchers, planners, decision-makers at the national, regional and local levels. Users: - General population, MINEO, MINTUR.

Adaptation actions

3 | Adaptation vision

Develop a database with geospatial representation of the tourism sector in Venezuela that makes it possible to assess vulnerability to climate change impacts, monitor it and develop specific adaptation strategies to increase the recovery capacity of the tourism sector in the face of extreme events related to climate change.

4 | Value proposition

Generation of a geographic database on climate conditions, ecosystems and natural resources in the regions of the country, which will allow the assessment, planning and management of tourism destinations and the simulation of risk scenarios for the tourism sector in the face of climate change. In order to identify the most vulnerable areas within the tourism sector and design climate change adaptation strategies.

5 | Adaptation options

Development of a database with geospatial representation of the tourism sector.

6 | Key activities

  • Design of a database with geospatial representation.
  • Training of technical staff in the use of the database with geospatial representation.
  • Data collection and processing and creation of vulnerability indicators.
  • Analysis of vulnerability to climate change in the tourism sector.

7 | Type of adaptation options and measures

The Development of a database with geospatial representation is considered a social information-generation option and an enabling measure aimed at reducing the sector's vulnerability to climate change.

Governance for adaptation

8 | Benefits and co-benefits

  • Protection of the ecosystems and biological diversity that form part of the tourism sector.
  • Reduction of the magnitude of the impacts of extreme climate events and greater resilience of the tourism sector and local communities.

9 | Key metrics

Indicators:

  • Validated, georeferenced and consolidated maps of the most vulnerable tourism destinations by region.
  • Summary report of vulnerable tourism destinations, including their respective regional maps. Targets (2025-2030):
  • 4 georeferenced and consolidated maps of the most vulnerable tourism destinations by region.
  • Summary report of vulnerable tourism destinations.

10 | Key actors

MINTUR, MINEC, Tour operators, General population.

11 Budget and costs

176.000 US$.

12 | Sources of financing (current or future)

  • Institutional financing.
  • External financing
